Mr President, honourable Members, thank you for the opportunity to discuss this crucial issue. The persistent crisis in Gaza and in Palestine more broadly obliged us to act. During my recent visit to Ramallah, I met Palestinian Vice-President al-Sheikh and Prime Minister Mustafa. The Palestinian Authority finances were under pressure, which affected the banking sector and access to finance of the private sector.

I see some positive further steps from the Israeli side. As you know, the corresponding banking arrangements have lately been extended every two weeks. This morning, we were informed that these arrangements have been extended until the end of 2026, which is another positive sign.

Basic services such as healthcare are challenged. Rising settler violence is straining all this further. During my visit to Israel, I underlined that our partnership requires a continued open and frank dialogue. Both President Herzog and Foreign Minister Sa'ar agreed and reiterated the importance of EU-Israeli relations. We need to engage with all parties. It is important that they engage with all European interlocutors as well.

Supporting a reformed Palestinian Authority and continuing to engage with Israel are not mutually exclusive. Without a buy-in from both sides, we will not be able to deliver on our objectives; early recovery in Gaza and the financial stability of a reformed Palestinian Authority. As I spoke to Israeli Foreign Minister Sa'ar, I told him the European Union remains strong in our support of a viable Palestinian state. There can be no just and lasting peace without it. I insisted on our collective interest in avoiding backsliding on the implementation of the Gaza peace plan, in line with the implementation of UN Secretary resolution 2803.

Early recovery in Gaza must start now, together with much more humanitarian assistance to meet the basic needs of civilians. We achieved an important step – Minister Sa'ar is open – or was open, has been open – for the European Union and its partners to initiate two critical early recovery interventions, one on solid waste management and another on water and sanitation.

This paves the way for the Palestinian donor group next week, on Monday 13 July, which I will co-chair with Prime Minister Mustafa. We are planning to bring together more than 65 delegations. We will be informed about the reform progress of the Palestinian Authority. We will also launch the Team Gaza initiative – the European Union, together with like-minded partners for early recovery in Gaza.

It is true – the situation is dire, but we are achieving real, concrete results with our diplomatic work.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, oggi la comunità internazionale è chiamata ad affrontare due sfide inseparabili.

La prima è garantire un'assistenza umanitaria immediata alla popolazione civile, la seconda è fare in modo che il 7 ottobre resti confinato alla storia e non torni mai più a segnare il futuro del Medio Oriente.

La prima impone di assicurare un accesso umanitario pieno, sicuro e senza ostacoli, affinché gli aiuti raggiungano rapidamente chi ne ha bisogno, senza essere intercettati o strumentalizzati da organizzazioni terroristiche.

La seconda richiede una visione politica di lungo periodo. La ricostruzione di Gaza dovrà accompagnarsi allo smantellamento delle reti terroristiche e ogni forma di estremismo che ha alimentato l'odio e la violenza.

L'Europa deve guidare questo processo mobilitando gli strumenti già disponibili per ricostruire ospedali, scuole e infrastrutture essenziali e creare le condizioni per una crescita economica e duratura, perché dalla stabilità di Gaza passa anche la stabilità del Mediterraneo, e dalla stabilità del Mediterraneo passa una parte decisiva della sicurezza e della prosperità dell'Europa.

paragraphs.text: A Uachtaráin, the people of Gaza have now suffered more than 1 000 days of genocide, 1 000 days of mass murder, starvation and an international community that's too cowardly to hold Israel accountable. The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestine Territory has found that Israel continues to commit genocide and deliberately targets Palestinian children in Gaza and the West Bank.

This is the rogue State that, according to the European Commission, is a close ally – this rogue State! We stand here and we talk about reconstruction and pretend that the genocide is over, when it continues. We need sanctions, a two-way arms embargo, suspension of the association agreement, a ban on trade with the illegal settlements and full, unequivocal support for UNWRA.

Before we even talk about reconstruction in Gaza, how about we talk about the fact that Israel has destroyed at least EUR 150 million of EU-funded infrastructure, and has not paid back a single cent? When is the Commission going to recover our taxpayers' money? When are they going to release the documents that relate to the destruction of EU-funded infrastructure in Gaza? Because the public has a right to know how much Israel is costing them.

Finally, the EU must urgently act to secure the immediate release of Doctor Hussam Abu Safiya, who has been arbitrarily detained by Israel since December 2024. He has been beaten, he has been tortured, he is at risk of death – free Doctor Hussam Abu Safiya!

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, Europe has been engaged for decades in providing humanitarian aid and basic social services to the people of Gaza. Recent initiatives by Commissioner Šuica, including the convening of donor conferences, demonstrate Europe's continued strong commitment, even at a time when equally devastating humanitarian catastrophes in Sudan, Yemen and Afghanistan demand our attention.

But reconstruction cannot simply mean rebuilding buildings. It must mean building a future in which Hamas can never again use civilian infrastructure as a base for terror, store weapons in schools or hospitals, or divert international assistance for its own extremist Islamist purposes. The reality is that Hamas has never respected and never will respect international law. On the contrary, its ideology is built on a cult of death and martyrdom in which individual human lives are meaningless, and the highest civilian death toll is cynically exploited to preserve its grip on power.

For us Europeans and for our partner Israel, international law matters because we have committed ourselves to it. But it is also clear that international law alone does not always provide solutions when dealing with terrorist organisations or violent and oppressive regimes. This is why we must urgently advance the implementation of the political process laid down in UN Security Council Resolution 2803.

Hamas announcing its withdrawal from Gaza's civil administration opens a critical window. The apolitical, technocratic National Committee for the Administration of Gaza can assume its responsibilities. The EU police training mission can help restore public order and improve security for civilians. And the CMCC is fully operational to coordinate stabilisation and relief efforts.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, while Israel continues with oppression and occupation, generations of Palestinians are paying the price. Yet every time until now, our European Union has failed to act properly.

Too many in this House, especially in the centre-right and the far-right side, chose to see nothing, hear nothing and say nothing. And you play the fourth monkey, through crossing your arms and thinking that you are not doing any evil. Let me be clear: inaction is action, and that choice has consequences. You even attack vital organisations such as UNRWA with baseless allegations, making yourself Netanyahu's and Hamas's useful idiots.

The EU does not suffer from a lack of solutions; the EU suffers from a lack of political courage. What more should Israel do for enough to be enough? Should it commit the genocide? Let me remind you: it has already done that. Can we start acting now and suspend the EU-Israel Association Agreement?
Commissioner, with all due respect, I don't know what steps you mean the Israeli Government has taken. The only steps I have seen until now are steps into other countries.

Maar we kunnen Israël toch onmogelijk verwijten dat ze probeert Hamas onder controle te krijgen? Dat brengt ons bij de kern van het probleem: de weigering van Hamas om de wapens neer te leggen. Hoe kan de EU dan helpen bij de wederopbouw? Ik zou willen zeggen: laten we ons daarbij concentreren op Hamasvrije gebieden. Zorg er in ieder geval voor dat er geen euro in handen komt van Hamas, want zolang deze terroristische organisatie er nog de lakens uitdeelt, blijft de situatie zoals die nu is volstrekt uitzichtloos.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, I was asking myself what kind of a charade is this? Rebuilding Gaza, really? For 1 000 days, the Palestinians in Gaza have been enduring unimaginable suffering, and they have not even elected the despicable terrorist organisation Hamas, still, they are paying the price for this narrative that is broadcasted in Europe – somehow it is still connected.

1 000 days of killings, even during the so-called ceasefire! Nothing seems to get a grip on us as Europeans. We are still unable to take any concrete action. Why haven't we suspended the agreement with Israel? Why haven't we forbidden imports from illegal settlements? Why haven't we acted? We still just speak these big words while 73 000 Palestinians have been killed, children have lost their limbs in thousands and many of them have been operated on without anaesthesia. Somewhere there has to be a heart – even in you, even in you! Somewhere there has to be a heart.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, grand statements do not resolve complex crises. It has been nine months since Trump declared a ceasefire for Gaza. Since then, more than 1 000 Palestinians have been killed and more than 60 % of Gaza is controlled by the Israeli military – with Netanyahu pushing for 70 % – and families forced to flee again and again.

An illegitimate so-called 'peace board' is to govern Gaza, without any role for Palestinians. Rafah never fully reopened, aid deliveries still severely restricted: this is not peace. This is war disguised as peace – and Netanyahu wants to keep it this way.

So where is Europe? How much longer will we hide behind constructive dialogue, when all it has delivered is nothing? The Commission put measures on the table almost a year ago: partial suspension of the Association Agreement, sanctions, trade measures. Let's finally take these steps and stop treating the status quo as a solution. Because it's not!

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Christian Democrats, dear Christian patriots, dear leaders of the EU, you are hypocrites. And you will probably end in hell. It is the Vatican, not me, who is saying: 'If a country is an enemy, it is condemned as undemocratic and sanctioned in various ways; but if it is an ally, the fact that it lacks freedom of expression, human rights or democracy is ignored.'
The EU chose as an ally the genocidal regime of Netanyahu. By doing that, we alienated the majority of Global South, including the Arab world, and lost any credibility regarding international law.

Please note that I don't speak about Israel or about the Jews. It is not about a country, and it is not at all about race. It is about a genocidal regime. The EU should denounce Netanyahu and his ministers as war criminals, which they are, now, or bear the mark of Cain of utter hypocrisy.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, my dear colleagues, reconstruction is an important step towards providing the people of Gaza with the prospect of returning to a semblance of normal life. Hopefully, it is soon possible.

The EU conducted an assessment in April, together with the World Bank and the United Nations, finding out that we would need USD 71.4 billion to rebuild the Palestinian enclave. Reconstruction must go far beyond rebuilding roads, hospitals and schools. It must restore hope and the foundation of a lasting peace.

The European Union is already the largest humanitarian donor to the Palestinians – it has to be mentioned. However, its construction also needs accountability. Therefore, I think the terror organisation of Hamas cannot play any role in the future of Gaza. The European Union must still support its two-state solution, enabling Palestine and Israel to coexist.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, yesterday, Hamas announced that it had dissolved its own government and had agreed to give up its role into the hands of the Palestinian Authority. It's the beginning of a big change yet doubts and fear in this moment are bigger than satisfaction in the Middle East.

The fear is that Hamas is going to apply the Hezbollah model: separation between administration and military wing. The suspicion is sustained by the fact that it has said nothing about the future of the military wing. On the other hand, the Board of Peace is a lost case – it has proved to be an ineffective, slow institution.

So I think these things can work in this moment. It is a very critical moment – new protagonists, new power, new country. Europe, especially, should act very fast and insert itself into this process. So it's time for Europe to step up, but very fast, Commissioner, with an independent, fully diplomatic initiative. We have the contacts, the people and the money to get it.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear leftists, when you talk about accountability, perhaps you should first look at yourselves. For years, you have been very consistent in your support for terrorist-led regime, demanding impossible standards of proof from Israel while accepting Hamas propaganda without any scepticism.

Let me be absolutely clear: Europe must never spend a single euro rebuilding what Hamas will simply use for the next war. We have already once paid for tunnels, rocket infrastructure and a terrorist regime.

So if you want accountability under international law, start with the organisation that started the war and massacred civilians. Before you say another word about reconstruction, make sure first that the Islamist terrorists are wiped out for good.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, a few months ago, I stood in the occupied West Bank, and around me was the rubble of what was once a community centre. The family next door were next – their house was next to go. And right there, there was still a children's playground with a shiny blue EU plaque. I wonder how many of those plaques are buried under the destruction of the genocide in Gaza.

Israel has destroyed more than EUR 150 million of EU-funded infrastructure there and in the West Bank, and the reconstruction of Gaza might cost up to EUR 70 billion in the next decade. When will we demand that Israel pay for the destruction that they caused? Yes, we must act swiftly to ensure humanitarian aid and reconstruct Gaza – we need to do this together with Palestinians and by recognising the irreplaceable role of UNWRA. But without accountability, we risk rebuilding today what Israel will destroy again tomorrow.

It's time for accountability – on Monday, finally, stop trade with illegal settlements, suspend the association agreement, introduce proper sanctions and support the ICC, because words will not rebuild Gaza, only actions will.

Ci sono migliaia di esseri umani che restano intrappolati in un campo di morte a cielo aperto, uccisi dalla fame, dalle malattie oppure dalle bombe democratiche di Tel Aviv.

Per salvare la dignità dell'Unione c'è una sola via: sospendere l'accordo di associazione con Israele e sanzionare il governo Netanyahu. Il resto è solo vergognosa ipocrisia.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, γενοκτονία με πάνω από 73.000 νεκρούς Παλαιστινίους, ισοπέδωση Γάζας, σχέδιο διαμελισμού και γενικευμένος εποικισμός στη Δυτική Όχθη με ιστορικό υψηλό δολοφονίας παιδιών: ατιμώρητα κατά συρροή εγκλήματα του κράτους κατακτητή Ισραήλ, με επίθεση επιπλέον στο Ιράν και εισβολή στον Λίβανο και τη Συρία.

Παράλληλα, επιβραβεύετε με προκλητική ασυλία επισκέψεις σαν της Επιτροπής στο Ισραήλ, στρατιωτικές και εμπορικές συμφωνίες από τις συνένοχες Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες, Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, ΝΑΤΟ και την ελληνική κυβέρνηση. Το αμερικανικό σχέδιο δήθεν ειρήνης, όπως και το αντίστοιχο ΝΑΤΟϊκό σχέδιο «Πύλη της Ανατολικής Μεσογείου», που μεθοδεύτηκε στη σύναξη στην Άγκυρα, προωθούν τους ενεργειακούς εμπορικούς διαύλους ευρωατλαντικών συμφερόντων στον ανταγωνισμό με Κίνα και Ρωσία.

Παρ' όλα αυτά, οι εξελίξεις απέδειξαν ότι ο ιμπεριαλισμός δεν είναι άτρωτος. Δεν είστε παντοδύναμοι, γιατί ούτε τον παλαιστινιακό λαό ούτε αυτόν του Ιράν βάλατε στο χέρι. Με τη διεθνιστική αλληλεγγύη και την αυτοτελή του πάλη, ο παλαιστινιακός λαός έχει τη δύναμη να επιβάλει το δίκιο του για ανεξάρτητο παλαιστινιακό κράτος με πρωτεύουσα την Ανατολική Ιερουσαλήμ στα σύνορα του '67.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señorías, reconstruir Gaza no es solamente dedicar recursos para volver a hacerla habitable —que también—, sino cómo hacemos para que los palestinos y las palestinas sean los únicos dueños y gobernantes de ese territorio. Cómo hacemos, cómo actúa y presiona Europa para que Gaza no se convierta en un resort de lujo para millonarios sin empatía ni vergüenza.

Gaza no es tierra de nadie, es parte de la nación palestina y, por lo tanto, solo corresponde a palestinos y palestinas decidir, comenzando por los términos de la reconstrucción y acabando con el ejercicio del derecho a decidir, con el derecho de autodeterminación del pueblo de Palestina.

Cualquier otro que se arrogue esa competencia en sustitución del pueblo palestino siempre contará con nuestro rechazo y nuestra denuncia. Y esa debiera ser también la actitud de la Unión en defensa de la legalidad internacional.

A fecha de hoy, Palestina sigue siendo objeto de un genocidio planificado que ha costado más de 70 000 vidas. Situarse del lado correcto de la historia exige suspender inmediatamente el Acuerdo de Asociación UE-Israel y dar cobertura política a la Corte Penal Internacional, particularmente en lo referente a las órdenes de detención contra los perpetradores del genocidio palestino.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Irgendwie haben alle Vorredner so ein bisschen recht, aber das wird den Menschen in Gaza tatsächlich nicht helfen. Der Aufbau – und da sind wir uns, glaube ich, alle klar – wird nur im Rahmen einer für alle Beteiligten politischen, grundsätzlichen Befriedung des Konfliktes möglich sein. Der EU fällt dabei die Rolle des zentralen finanziellen und diplomatischen Unterstützers zu, während Israel nach dem Völkerrecht als Besatzungsmacht primär für die Versorgung und den Wiederaufbau ziviler Infrastruktur verantwortlich wäre. In der Realität passiert genau das Gegenteil – und Frieden liegt in der Ferne.

Unterdessen muss die EU weiterhin in Zusammenarbeit mit allen Akteuren versuchen, humanitäre Hilfe nach Gaza zu bringen, und versuchen, die Verletzten des Gazakrieges zu retten. Wir sollten überlegen, ob wir die Mittel für die Grenzmission Rafah schnell in die Krankenhäuser von West Bank und Jordanien umleiten, um praktische Hilfe leisten zu können.
Letzte Woche war ich Zeuge der Evakuierung von Verletzten und Angehörigen über Jordanien nach Spanien und die Türkei. Danke Spanien, danke Jordanien, danke der Türkei!
Seien wir die EU, die für die Schwachen, die Entrechteten, die Betrogenen und die leidenden Verletzten die Völkerfamilie ist, die sich kümmert!

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! EU är den största givaren till den palestinska myndigheten, och inför nästa veckas möte i den palestinska givargruppen måste det vara glasklart att ekonomiskt stöd förutsätter konkreta reformer. Utan resultat finns inga förutsättningar för en varaktig fred.

Först måste Hamas avväpnas och genomgripande avradikalisering genomföras i Gaza. Skolundervisningen måste reformeras så att antisemitism, glorifiering av terrorism och martyrskap inte traderas till nästa generation.
I fjol betalade PA ut motsvarande 156 miljoner US-dollar i ersättningar och förmåner till terrorister och deras familjer inom ramen för pay to slay. Också detta måste omedelbart upphöra.

Om dessa förhållanden inte förändras förblir tvåstatslösningen en illusion. Kommissionen måste vara glasklar: Uteblivna reformer kommer att få kännbara ekonomiska konsekvenser. Europeiska skattebetalares pengar ska aldrig användas för att finansiera eller belöna terrorism.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, à Gaza, le cessez-le-feu n’existe que sur le papier. Les frappes continuent. Elles tuent 125 Palestiniens chaque mois. L’armée israélienne ne s’est pas retirée; elle contrôle 60 % de la bande de Gaza.

Alors, dans ce Parlement, il faut que notre groupe insiste à chaque plénière pour que nous puissions juste débattre de ce qu’il se passe en Palestine. Toute discussion est systématiquement verrouillée par les groupes de droite et d’extrême droite. Pourquoi? Comment être à ce point aveugle à la souffrance humaine et à l’injustice?

Cela a été dit: il a fallu quelques heures au gouvernement israélien pour rompre les relations avec la haute représentante de l’Union européenne, Kaja Kallas, parce qu’elle dénonçait le régime d’apartheid en Cisjordanie. Mais nous, nous tergiversons depuis des années, sans suspension de l’accord d’association avec Israël. Nous n’avons toujours pas condamné la loi sur le rétablissement de la peine de mort en Israël, conçue pour ne s’appliquer qu’aux Palestiniens, toujours pas protégé la Cour pénale internationale contre les sanctions américaines.

Cette inaction complice est celle des droites européennes, que l’histoire jugera. Il y a des élections dans quelques mois en Palestine et en Israël. Une nouvelle génération peut arriver au pouvoir pour enfin travailler à la justice, à l’égalité des droits et à la paix. Il faut agir maintenant.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, international law is the foundation of peace and security. When we weaken it, we all become less secure. That is why, first, Europe should be sceptical of the so-called Board of Peace. Lasting peace depends on strong institutions and clear rules that provide legitimacy, predictability and accountability. Europe should never accept their replacement by alternative and personalised structures that lack a sound foundation in international law.

Second, the same principles must guide our approach to Gaza. We should support Israel's right to self-defence. At the same time, all violations of international humanitarian law must be investigated and those responsible held accountable. The independence of the International Criminal Court should be respected. Advisory opinions of the International Court of Justice have to be respected as well.
Third, the reconstruction of Gaza cannot succeed while Hamas remains an armed force. It has no role in Gaza's future. The real test is not declarations, but genuine disarmament.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, volete sapere come possiamo opporci e garantire la ricostruzione di Gaza, la pace?

Le Nazioni Unite ce l'hanno detto: Israele ha deliberatamente ucciso bambini, Israele sta compiendo un genocidio.

E dove sono, ora, questi criminali? Sono a Gaza. Decidono cosa entra e cosa esce, chi entra e chi esce. Sono in Cisgiordania, dove fanno accordi con i coloni per rubare le terre dei palestinesi, catturarli e ucciderli brutalmente.
Israele sta illegalmente occupando Gaza e la Cisgiordania. Nel frattempo, i palestinesi a Gaza continuano a morire tra i topi, senza acqua, tra le rovine, sotto le bombe, tra i corpi dei loro cari.
E noi che facciamo? Continuiamo a fare affari con dei criminali di guerra, con un governo genocida, continuiamo a trattarli come alleati.
Basta! Dobbiamo interrompere i rapporti con Israele.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, this crisis must not be forgotten. Hamas is still around in Gaza. It is not yet gone. People are still under pressure. This terrorist organisation even was not ashamed to put children on the line, to put women on the line, to put their own civil society, the civil population, at risk. And they are still around.

So I can only one more time advocate for deweaponising the terrorist organisation, demilitarising Gaza, creating proper education towards a proper civil society without hatred, antisemitism, Islamism, creating a precondition for economic self-capability so that one day it will not be necessary anymore that the whole world pours money into the region.

And when development aid is given, not one single cent must be misused for hatred, for Islamism, for antisemitism, because that means pouring hatred into even children's hearts, which leads again to such an outrageous violence such as in 7 October.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, hoe kan deze Commissie zichzelf nog in de ogen kijken. Hoe doen onze regeringsleiders dat eigenlijk? Terwijl Gaza levend wordt begraven en de Westelijke Jordaanoever wordt opgeslokt, nederzetting per nederzetting. En dat in real time voor onze ogen. En laten we ook stoppen met te zeggen dat dit een ingewikkeld verhaal is. Dat is het niet. Het geweld is onwettig, de bezetting is onwettig, de nederzettingen zijn illegaal.

De Verenigde Naties zeggen ons dat, het Internationaal Gerechtshof heeft het gezegd en ook vanuit de Europese Unie moet dat luid en duidelijk blijven klinken. En toch gebeurt er niets. En dat heeft een naam: medeplichtigheid. Schors dat associatieverdrag volledig, verbiedt de handel in producten uit illegale nederzettingen en breidt die sancties uit. Deze Commissie wilde ooit een geopolitieke Commissie zijn. Europa wil een belangrijke rol spelen op het geopolitieke toneel. Wel, doe dan iets. Woorden volstaan niet. Free Palestine. Nu.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, humanitarian aid has been weaponised and politicised, 90 % of Gaza destroyed, 60 % of Gaza occupied, continual encroachments into the West Bank, aggressive actions by settlers being facilitated by the Netanyahu government and the Israeli Defence Forces. Fundamental breaches of international law, refusal to accept decisions of the International Criminal Court. At the same time, we are here in the House today debating the EU's role and reconstruction of the Gaza Strip and accountability of Israel under international law.

But maybe it's time that we started looking for accountability among ourselves, because we have consistently turned a blind eye to Israel in all its actions with regard to Palestine. No acceptance of the two-state solution, no acceptance of the Palestinians' right to self-determination.

Israel acts with impunity because we have granted it immunity. We simply will never sanction any action that Israel does. So the accountability should start here in this House, in the European Union, and particularly among the Council.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora comisaria, le tengo que confesar algo. Tras Gaza, tras mil días de genocidio, yo soy otra persona. Nadie puede convivir con tanto horror sin cambiar su forma de estar en el mundo, de verse a sí mismo y a la humanidad.

Hoy debatimos sobre Israel, pero en realidad debatimos sobre nosotros. Sucedió y puede volver a suceder. Nos lo advirtió Primo Levi después de Auschwitz. ¿Y nosotros qué le dijimos? No, nunca más... lo prometimos. Mentimos. Está volviendo a suceder. Y ustedes se hacen fotos con los responsables.

¿Somos mejores que aquellos que miraron a otro lado cuando deportaban a judíos como Primo Levi? Somos peores, porque ahora no podemos decir que no sabíamos, ni tan siquiera que no participábamos. Cuando nos preguntamos por quién doblan las campanas, doblan por nosotros.

¿Qué será de nosotros después de Gaza, señora comisaria? Los lugares más oscuros del infierno nos esperan: a la derecha —que hoy no está aquí— por su participación en el genocidio, por deshumanizarse, y a nosotros por no impedirlo.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária Šuica, enquanto discutimos a reconstrução de Gaza, a destruição no terreno continua.

O cessar-fogo é uma mentira. Israel continua a assassinar palestinianos, a impedir a entrada da ajuda humanitária de que necessitam, a atacar acampamentos de palestinianos desalojados, a destruir infraestruturas civis, algumas delas construídas com financiamento da União Europeia.

Enquanto aqui discutimos a responsabilização de Israel pelas violações do direito internacional, a União Europeia mantém a sua plena cumplicidade com o genocídio. A Senhora Comissária foi a Israel para reafirmar que as relações políticas, económicas e até de cooperação militar com Israel se mantêm a todo o vapor: a prova mais evidente da cumplicidade da União Europeia com o genocídio está aqui.
Nem o relatório da Comissão de Inquérito das Nações Unidas, que denuncia o genocídio e os crimes cometidos por Israel contra as crianças, faz a União Europeia corar de vergonha e reverter o caminho.
Mas esse tem de ser o sentido: garantir o respeito pelos direitos do povo palestiniano, pôr fim ao genocídio.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, the situation in Gaza is dire. But we must also draw attention to the situation of the West Bank, where Israeli forces are actively cooperating with the violent settlers, ignoring court decisions and international law, and facilitating attacks on innocent Palestinian families. From the beginning of the war, settlers and the IDF have killed at least 1 160 Palestinians in the West Bank, including 242 children – children, colleagues, while simply living on their own land.

This is why I strongly condemn any tolerance and support for Israeli violations, including dangerous threats by the new Slovenian Government and President of the Government Janez Janša, member of the EPP, to move the Slovenian embassy to Jerusalem. This not only shows the one-eighty overnight shift in Slovenian foreign policy but also deviates from the official EU position.
Colleagues, the EU will retake a test of principles on Monday. To pass, we must suspend the EU‑Israel Association Agreement.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Mr President, before I came to this Parliament, I was a schoolteacher in Germany. And back in my home country, we make sure children deeply study the darkest chapter of our past so they never, ever question the horrors of what happened.

But we only succeed as educators if we get students to think beyond the specifics of one era. Because that's exactly what people do to avoid accountability: they hide behind the specifics of the moment to justify looking away at today's crimes.

But history is not a museum piece; it's a life lesson in human dignity. And the hardest part is recognising suffering when it wears a different face in a different era. True reconstruction begins with the courage to apply international law equally. If we don't ask for accountability now from the perpetrator of this genocide, we have failed the most fundamental lesson of our recent history.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, we praten over de wederopbouw van Gaza alsof er een natuurramp heeft plaatsgehad. Maar de realiteit is anders: als onderdeel van een genocidale campagne heeft Israël 85 % van Gaza met de grond gelijk gemaakt. Er is op papier een staakt‑het‑vuren, dus zou wederopbouw mogelijk moeten zijn en zou humanitaire hulp mogelijk moeten zijn. Maar dat verhult de werkelijkheid. Ook zijn sinds dat staakt‑het‑vuren meer dan duizend Palestijnen gedood en duizenden gewonden gevallen. En de hulp die wel binnenkomt is onvoldoende en aan banden gelegd met absurde beperkingen. Protheses worden tegengehouden als militaire middelen. Deze week nog werden hulpverleners blootgesteld aan luchtaanvallen. Onder zulke omstandigheden is het onmogelijk om te spreken over wederopbouw en een fatsoenlijk gesprek daarover te hebben. Het beleid van de Israëlische regering is niet veranderd. Zolang Europa dit blindelings laat gebeuren, is trots praten over de Europese inzet voor wederopbouw en humanitaire hulp niets meer dan een schaamlap. Het Palestijnse volk verdient wederopbouw en humanitaire hulp. Daarom moet het Associatieverdrag tussen de EU en Israël worden opgeschort.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, sono stato con altri parlamentari nella Cisgiordania, nei territori occupati.

Abbiamo visto, appena arrivati nella città di Hebron, una curva dove ci è stato indicato che c'erano ancora delle macchie di sangue di alcuni palestinesi uccisi qualche giorno prima e abbiamo chiesto: "Ma perché non vi rivolgete alla giustizia?" "No, perché noi non abbiamo la giustizia normale. Noi abbiamo la giustizia militare, e la prima cosa che farebbero sarebbe venire a distruggere la nostra casa."

Ho visto un bambino che non aveva l'incubatrice: nato sottopeso, era in una scatola di scarpe con del cotone; una sposa che piangeva perché, dietro di lei, la sua casa era distrutta per motivi di sicurezza.
Non possiamo continuare in questo modo. Ho visto trattare esattamente quel popolo come sono stati trattati gli ebrei durante la Seconda guerra mondiale.
Dobbiamo sanzionare Israele, interrompere ogni contatto con Israele, perché Israele ascolta, in questo momento, con il suo governo, solo la forza.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, o Tribunal Internacional de Justiça foi claro: Israel tem obrigações. Tem de garantir o essencial à sobrevivência da população de Gaza. Tem de deixar entrar ajudas, sem exceções. Mais, o Tribunal rejeitou com factos as desculpas usadas para bloquear essas mesmas ajudas.

Uma decisão do Tribunal que não é cumprida não é só uma decisão ignorada. É o direito internacional posto em causa e quem viola o direito internacional tem de responder por isso perante a justiça e perante a História.
Não pode haver impunidade. Não pode haver regras para uns, exceções para outros. A História julgará não só aqueles que violaram direitos humanos, como aqueles que assistiram e nada disseram.
Basta de palavras sem consequências! É tempo de suspender o Acordo de Associação União Europeia-Israel!

Este doble estándar está destruyendo nuestra credibilidad y nuestra dignidad. Gaza ha pasado de ser una cárcel al aire libre —como decía Borrell— a un cementerio al aire libre. paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, Minister, you just saw a lucky mother with her excellent child. But unfortunately in Gaza the hospitals are destroyed. Hospitals are not battlefields; yet in Gaza, the basic principle of humanity has been broken for too long, colleagues.

Since the October ceasefire, the strikes have not stopped and humanitarian access remains conditional and obstructed, colleagues. I am speaking with you, the representatives from the Council, colleagues, now.
Children are dying not only from bombs, but from the collapse of hospitals and the healthcare system. Now you see the contrast between those two examples.

And of course, you know, this is not a side issue to the political debate. A ceasefire that still allows a hospital to run out of oxygen is not peace, it's a crime. And we need to stop it immediately. And it's up to us now to send a clear message to the Council: please act.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, dear colleagues, stability in the Middle East is of utmost importance. For European security and stability but, most importantly, of course, for the people who have been suffering too much and for too long. The only viable way to long-term stability is the two-state solution. What does this mean, a two-state solution? It means two fully democratic states holding regular and free elections, meaning no space for religious extremists on all sides. No Hamas nor Orthodox extremists, which also includes the settlers in the West Bank.

With the newest reports coming now from Gaza, a clear European position for a two-state solution is essential. We cannot leave rebuilding to the United States under Donald Trump. We need to stand on the side of human rights, of international law and the people hoping for peace and prosperity in this region.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, 73 000 Palestinians have been killed. Among them, 21 000 kids; 10 000 kids have suffered life-changing injuries; 60 000 kids have lost one or both of their parents. Hundreds of journalists have been killed. Hundreds of thousands of homes have been completely damaged or totally destroyed. So when this genocide is being perpetrated, settler violence still continues to this very day. Land is stolen. Families are beaten. Children are being terrorised.

Now, let's be honest: no horror will ever justify another. But what if these were Ukrainian kids or Ukrainian families? What if this genocide was being perpetrated by the Iranian regime? This Chamber would not be empty as it is today. It would roar. It would call it for what it is.

So please spare us the empty speeches, especially from the right side of this House, because there is no reconstruction without justice. There is no reconstruction without a Palestinian state. Israel has every right to exist, but so does Palestine. And recognising the right of the Palestinian people is no punishment against Israel; it is the rightful recognition of the Palestinian people. So end the EU-Israel Association Agreement now.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, a Gaza il genocidio non è mai finito.
Le parole del patriarca di Gerusalemme, Pizzaballa, sono come pietre: mancano acqua, cibo, medicinali, i topi mordono i bambini, mentre le persone muoiono.
Hamas sembra aprire al trasferimento dell'amministrazione civile, ma non al disarmo. E intanto si parla del dispiegamento di un contingente marocchino.
Il piano di Trump avanza nel vuoto lasciato dall'Europa, ma la ricostruzione di Gaza deve essere sotto l'egida delle Nazioni Unite e delle sue agenzie, come l'UNRWA.

Per questo serve dare messaggi netti ora, di fronte alla deriva del governo israeliano. Mi rivolgo al governo italiano in primis, a Giorgia Meloni: abbia il coraggio, per una volta, e tolga il veto sulla sospensione dell'accordo di associazione UE‑Israele, riconosca, come Italia, lo Stato di Palestina. È necessario che almeno la parte commerciale degli accordi sia sospesa, come abbiamo chiesto in questo Parlamento.
L'Europa rompa con il doppio standard e faccia ciò che serve per restituire dignità e libertà ai palestinesi.
Stop al genocidio, stop al terrorismo, stop alla violenza. Lavoriamo insieme per ricostruzione e pace.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Minister Byrne, I have a simple question: what do we mean when we say 'respect for human rights'? It is the foundation of our European project and a legal obligation under Article 2 of the EU-Israel Association Agreement. It doesn't mean the killing of tens of thousands of Palestinian children, reducing the city of Gaza to rubble, turning what's left into an open-air prison the world is forbidden to enter.

The list of Israel's crimes is endless, but I can name one action we need to take: ending the EU-Israel Association Agreement. Why does the agreement remain? It's worth billions to the Israeli economy. Yet we comfort ourselves by saying we will lead in rebuilding Gaza. But you cannot rebuild a hospital with one hand, while rewarding the war criminals that flattened us with the other.
Ending this agreement is not radical. It is the minimum required by our own law and our own values. The Irish Presidency of the EU must lead. End the EU-Israel Association Agreement once and for all!

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members who are left in this room, I was listening carefully to each of you, and I heard each word which you said during this meeting.

Our speaking slots are not enough to elaborate on this very difficult topic. One-minute speeches are not enough to discuss this topic. I have to say that I am here representing High Representative/Vice-President Kaja Kallas. So I will quote her first: 'The European Union and Israel have a lot that binds us together. I value our dialogue and engagement, respectfully and constructively. Dialogue is the foundation of diplomacy, especially when differences arise.' This is what our HR/VP said. So I'm building on this and leaning on this.

All of us know that the situation is dire. The topic is very serious, as I said. Listening to you, I felt like I was a rival in a Foreign Affairs Council. As long as we are divided, we will stay powerless. All of you turn to the Commission, turn to me. I don't want to blame anyone. This is not a black-and-white story; this is not a blame game. But the ball is with the Council. The Member who was speaking last, Mr Ó Ríordáin, really said the right thing. He was the only one who turned towards the Council. I am also looking towards the Council, and I think that during the Irish Presidency, I wish they would be capable of reaching consensus.

Unfortunately, the association agreement and its suspension is at the table as of last September, you remember. During the State of the Union speech, it was put on the table. Unfortunately, I was present at each and every Foreign Affairs Council – the Member States are divided. Not to blame anyone, but just to say there is a problem. We can speak for decades like this. We can blame each other. We can post our video clips blaming someone. But I say we won't reach a solution if we attack each other. This is not the way how it works. So I really hope that under the Irish Presidency, we will be capable of reaching the unanimity on this.

Someone said time to suspend the association agreement. Yes, time is to spend the association agreement, but it's on the table. And, as I told you, turning towards us and toward me was not the right address. We are trying to find a solution all the time. We are having a dialogue. In parallel, we are really financing the Palestinian Authority. Without us, all of you know that the Palestinian Authority would not have survived. Those people there – teachers, nurses, doctors – we have this package programme, which is EUR 1.6 billion. So without us, they would have collapsed.

paragraphs.text: I have replied to all of you. I especially want to thank Mr Sánchez Amor, because I need your support for this. In the next MFF, we want to have extra money on top of our budget. The Team Gaza initiative is being launched and we would like to have this in our budget. It is very important, but we cannot do it without you. You are the ones who decide on the budget in the end. So we are trying to bring together a coalition of all Member States, a coalition of the willing, and this is what we are doing.

But, as I said, each and every conflict ended at the negotiation table. We need conditions, we need circumstances for this. And, first of all, we need accession to Gaza. Unfortunately, this NCAG committee which was established sits in Cairo. At the moment they haven't acceded Gaza. This is what I was trying to do during my visit in Israel. As I told you in my introductory speech, they released now these banking sector issues, and they also approved the two projects for waste and water management, which I think is a good sign.
So we need diplomacy and we are doing what we can.

I hope that during this Palestine donor group, which will be held on Monday, there will be much more to say. So I want to thank you for all this and we need to be together. We need to be unified. This not a blame game. We have to help people on the ground.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you very much, and I want to thank all of the speakers who made their voices heard so strongly in this debate. I have noted that I think almost 50 Members have spoken in this debate and it shows the very strong views here in the European Parliament. The Council certainly takes note of everything that was said and I particularly mention, as the Commissioner did, Aodhán Ó Ríordáin, but also Mr Andriukaitis as well, for directly addressing the Council.

Diverging views have been expressed on what the EU can and should do to help the people in Gaza, and to hold Israel and Hamas accountable. But I can say this: we are united in one common goal, and that is lasting peace and security in the Middle East.

In our priorities as the Irish Presidency, which our Taoiseach presented yesterday, we have committed to promoting active engagement in support of such lasting peace and security regarding the conflicts in the Middle East, and in particular the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians. This reaffirms, and must reaffirm, the EU's commitment to a two-state solution, where both Israelis and Palestinians can live in peace and security.

We must work towards ending the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and the deteriorating situation in the West Bank. Next week, as I said already, the Council is looking forward to the options that the Commission will present for the meeting of the Foreign Affairs Council on 13 July in light, particularly, of the further deteriorating situation regarding the illegal settlements. I have no doubt that the Council and the members of the Council will certainly hear the views that have been expressed here in the European Parliament.

interventions.speaker_label: Costas Kadis, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, on 8 May, two Spanish Guardia Civil agents were killed after their boats collided while chasing suspected drug traffickers in the Atlantic. I feel deeply for the two officers, their relatives and their colleagues. This tragic event reminds us of the risks that law enforcement officers face to keep narcotics off our streets. They deserve our full support.

Honourable Members, we recently presented the annual European Drugs Report. It paints an alarming picture. Cocaine is more available than ever before. Between 2013 and 2023, cocaine seizures in Europe increased sixfold. At the same time, we are seeing a sharp rise in synthetic drugs, which are often even more dangerous and harder to detect.

Drug trafficking is not an isolated crime. It fuels money laundering, corruption, human trafficking, violence and other forms of serious organised crime. Behind this market are highly sophisticated criminal networks. They use advanced technologies, including for their communications, international logistics chains and enormous financial resources. At the same time, they exploit social vulnerabilities, social inclusion, lack of opportunities, mental health challenges and other societal pressures that create an environment in which drug use and addiction can flourish. That is why we take a comprehensive approach: the new EU drugs strategy combines public health preservation and treatment with a strong security and law enforcement response, because we need to reduce both supply and demand.

On the law enforcement side, we presented a European action plan against drug trafficking at the end of last year. Its objective is to target criminal networks along the entire supply chain, from production countries and transit routes to European markets. A key focus is the security of our ports. A large share of the cocaine entering Europe comes through them. That is why we are strengthening the European Ports Alliance, improving controls and tackling the infiltration of ports by organised crime. The alliance shows what can be achieved when public authorities and private operators work hand in hand, and you can see the results in the media: four tonnes of cocaine seized at Rotterdam in March, eight tonnes concealed in cocoa beans in Wilhelmshaven in May, and over 100 tonnes of cocaine and ketamine hidden in timber from Chile.

We are also stepping up cooperation with partner countries, particularly in Latin America. Drug trafficking is a global business and our response must be global as well. Europol has recently concluded new partnerships with Brazil and Ecuador to strengthen the fight against drug trafficking and organised crime. The Commission has recently proposed a new mandate for Europol; it will strengthen the agency as Europe's information hub, operational hub and technology hub, enabling it to better support Member States in tackling increasingly sophisticated criminal networks. And early next year, we will propose modernised rules on organised crime.
I encourage you to give priority to all these files in the coming months, so that we will be able to see their impact on the ground soon. I look forward to the discussions that will follow.

interventions.speaker_label: Ana Miguel Pedro, em nome do Grupo PPE.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, o narcotráfico marítimo no Atlântico está a evoluir rapidamente e pressiona cada vez mais as fronteiras da União Europeia. Falamos de redes mais organizadas, mais agressivas, mais sofisticadas, com impacto direto na nossa segurança interna e na nossa capacidade de resposta.

As operações recentes em Espanha e em Portugal, nas quais lamentamos a morte de agentes da Guardia Civil e da GNR, mostram que esta é uma ameaça estruturada e cada vez mais impune. Só em 2025 deixámos escapar cerca de 192 embarcações e 700 toneladas de cocaína no Atlântico. As redes adaptam-se: mudam de rota, usam a África Ocidental como ponto de transbordo, recorrem a embarcações de alta velocidade e a narcossubmarinos para redistribuir a droga por diferentes rotas. No mar, continuam a ter vantagem pela mobilidade, pelo alcance e pela rapidez de fuga.
A Comissão Europeia não pode limitar-se a acompanhar o fenómeno. Tem de liderar uma resposta operacional, legislativa e tecnológica à altura da ameaça.
Precisamos de mais financiamento, sim, mas precisamos sobretudo de mais capacidade, mais vigilância aérea, mais partilha de informação e de inteligência, mais instrumentos operacionais.

Precisamos também de rever com seriedade as regras de intervenção no mar, com uma abordagem clara sobre o uso proporcional da força em operações marítimas de alto risco. A Comissão deve ainda avançar com legislação europeia sobre a posse, a modificação e a operação de embarcações de alta potência utilizadas pelo crime organizado. Deve apoiar tecnologias capazes de neutralizar motores à distância e deve reforçar a cooperação com os Estados-Membros e com os países da África Ocidental, onde muitas destas rotas se consolidam.

Senhor Comissário, não podemos pedir às nossas forças de segurança que enfrentem organizações que não conhecem fronteiras com meios limitados, com regras desajustadas, com financiamento pensado para os desafios do século passado. Não podemos exigir eficácia sem lhes dar capacidade.
Esta é uma questão de segurança, de soberania e de Estado de direito.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Juan Fernando López Aguilar, en nombre del Grupo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario, llevamos dos años de legislatura del Parlamento Europeo y es raro el pleno —si es que hay alguno— que se libre de un punto en el que las fuerzas que hacen oposición al Gobierno de España no lo aprovechen instrumentalmente para criticarlo.

Resulta deplorable en un asunto tan sensible que debería concitar tanto nuestra unidad como es la lucha contra el narcotráfico en nuestras fronteras exteriores y el apoyo a las fuerzas y cuerpos de seguridad, que es exactamente lo que hace el Gobierno de España.

El ministro del Interior ha incrementado en 17 000 los policías y los guardias civiles —4 000 de ellos en Andalucía— durante el mandato del Gobierno progresista que preside Pedro Sánchez. Se han invertido 2 000 millones EUR en infraestructuras de comisarías y, por tanto, centros de seguridad en la zona del Campo de Gibraltar.

Evidentemente, este asunto tiene dimensión europea y, por tanto, lo que importa es la Estrategia de la UE sobre Drogas y el plan de acción de la UE contra el narcotráfico, con coordinación europea y en colaboración con Eurojust y con Europol.

Tal y como sugiere la Agencia de la Unión Europea sobre Drogas —situada en Lisboa—, tiene que haber una partida europea para recursos europeos y, por supuesto, la protección de víctimas. Debemos ponernos del lado de las víctimas sin hacernos jamás la foto con los narcotraficantes.

interventions.speaker_label: Hermann Tertsch, en nombre del Grupo PfE.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, el narcotráfico no es solo un enemigo terrible para la salud de los individuos y sociedades, hoy el narcotráfico es, además, un arma de guerra híbrida y un poder político colosal.

El crimen organizado ha entrado en la política. Hace décadas, los carteles de la droga se aliaron con la izquierda iberoamericana. Hoy, ese narcosocialismo del Foro de São Paulo ya está en Europa y entró por España. El Gobierno de Sánchez liquidó a las mejores unidades de policía antidrogas y las otras, sin medios, son impotentes. De ahí los muertos por las ventajas de los narcos que ha provocado el propio Gobierno español.

España es hoy el paraíso de los narcos gracias al Gobierno amigo. Primero, porque están abiertas todas las costas y, después, porque campan a sus anchas y porque invierten y blanquean su dinero en España.
La única forma de frenar el narcotráfico es acabar con los Gobiernos que trabajan para él; es decir, acabar con el socialismo —con el narcosocialismo— es la clave para acabar con esta plaga.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, per troppo tempo le istituzioni hanno trattato il narcotraffico, lo spaccio e il consumo di droga come un male endemico, ormai non più estirpabile, quasi invincibile, a volte da arginare, se non, nelle peggiori delle ipotesi, addirittura da ignorare o favorire.

Se vogliamo, invece, essere responsabili come persone impegnate in politica, dobbiamo dimostrare di avere un cuore aperto alla coscienza e al bene comune. Dobbiamo crederci, crederci fermamente, dobbiamo credere nel fatto che queste reti criminali possono essere sconfitte e possono essere sconfitti coloro che guadagnano sulla pelle dei più giovani e sulla morte delle persone.

E se è così, allora abbiamo il compito, il dovere, di dare gli strumenti adeguati alle nostre forze dell'ordine e di investire maggiori risorse. Dobbiamo imporre ai porti maggiori e costanti controlli, difendere i confini e usare il pugno di ferro.
Questo è l'unico modo per vincere contro i trafficanti di morte. Non possiamo infatti lasciare soli coloro che combattono, da soli, in prima linea.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, the convicted and wanted drug lord Jos Leijdekkers remains free because Sierra Leone refuses to extradite him. One month ago, I called on the European Commission to increase pressure on Sierra Leone after the largest seizure of cocaine in the Canary Islands. The Netherlands has already made repeated requests through all available diplomatic and legal channels. Yet Sierra Leone continues to refuse cooperation. In fact, it appears to be shielding Jos Leijdekkers and even facilitating drug trafficking. This must stop now.

Drug-related organised crime undermines our security, trust in the rule of law and ultimately threatens our democracy. All European countries should therefore take this seriously and stand united in the fight against organised crime. The European Union must come forward with a concrete and comprehensive package of measures, including suspension of EU development cooperation with countries that refuse to cooperate in the extradition of convicted criminals. I ask the Commissioner: what is the current state of this confrontation and when can we expect ...

interventions.speaker_label: Leoluca Orlando, a nome del gruppo Verts/ALE.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, l'Europa attrae e consuma enormi quantità di sostanze stupefacenti in un mercato di droghe miliardario.
L'Europa è diventata luogo di incontro tra narcotraffico colombiano, narcomafie europee e italiane e organizzazioni criminali belghe, olandesi, francesi e altre.

Questo criminale mercato si alimenta anche di produzione di droga in paesi dell'Asia – dal Laos al Myanmar, dall'Afghanistan al Pakistan – con il recente allarme dell'ONU sulla provenienza di droghe sintetiche da est.

Una rete di complicità rende possibile eludere i controlli di polizia nei maggiori porti europei. Non basta accertare l'identità di quanti attraversano il Mediterraneo e l'Atlantico, è urgente intervenire e intercettare all'origine gli accordi criminali tra cartelli nello smercio verso l'Europa.

Urge, in sede di loro prevista riforma, signor Commissario, rafforzare Europol ed Eurojust nella loro lotta alla criminalità organizzata, per offrire una risposta europea forte. C'è inoltre bisogno di maggiore coordinamento per contrastare il riciclaggio dei profitti del narcotraffico tramite sistemi bancari e finanziari europei.
Considerando gli effetti che questo riciclaggio di denaro ha nella vita...

interventions.speaker_label: Mary Khan, im Namen der ESN-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Europa steht vor einer Explosion der Drogenkriminalität, und wir erleben eine Rekordverfügbarkeit illegaler Drogen. Die EU hat die USA inzwischen als größten Kokainmarkt überholt, und bei Eurojust sind die Fallzahlen in nur fünf Jahren – nur fünf Jahren – um 60 % gestiegen; Drogen im Wert von 20 Mrd. EUR wurden festgestellt. Mehr als die Hälfte der gefährlichsten kriminellen Netzwerke Europas sind im Drogenschmuggel tätig, zwei Drittel setzen Gewalt ein, über 70 % nutzen Korruption, um Behörden und Hafenpersonal zu beeinflussen.

Das ist keine Randerscheinung mehr; das ist ein sicherheitspolitisches Totalversagen. Selbst Europol stellt fest: Die Netzwerke, die Drogen nach Europa schmuggeln, sind häufig dieselben kriminellen Strukturen, die auch illegale Migration und Menschenhandel organisieren. Die Kartelle haben längst verstanden: Europas offene Grenzen und politische Kuschelkurse sind ihr Geschäftsmodell.

Unsere Häfen dürfen nicht länger Einfallstore für Drogenkartelle sein, und unsere Grenzen dürfen nicht länger Geschäftsmodelle für Schleuser sein. Die Lösung ist so simpel und heißt: Außengrenzen sichern, Schleusernetzwerke zerschlagen und illegale Migration stoppen.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señorías, el narcotráfico mata: mata a quienes consumen, mata el futuro de los jóvenes, mata el Estado de Derecho y mata a los agentes que lo combaten.

Los guardias civiles asesinados en Huelva y Barbate arrollados por narcolanchas no son una tragedia aislada, son la consecuencia de años de impunidad, de falta de recursos de un Gobierno como el de Sánchez, que desprotege a las fuerzas de seguridad, que liquida OCON-Sur —la unidad clave en la lucha contra el narco—.

Europol lo ha advertido: los narcotraficantes ya no solo introducen la droga desde fuera de la Unión Europea, sino que están infiltrados en Europa. Operan desde nuestros puertos, blanquean capitales con empresas pantalla y usan armas de guerra y tecnología punta para corromper, intimidar y matar.

Europa, comisario, acierta con la Alianza Europea de Puertos, persiguiendo el dinero y cortando el oxígeno financiero de las bandas, pero el nuevo marco estratégico solo funcionará si protegemos a quienes nos protegen, tipificamos el eurodelito a cada ataque a cada policía, reconocemos la profesión de riesgo de nuestros policías.

El narcotráfico es la mayor amenaza para la seguridad de Europa y debemos estrechar la cooperación entre Europol, Eurojust, Frontex, Aduanas y las policías nacionales. Debemos exigir a cada Estado más compromiso, más agentes, más medios, más seguridad jurídica y una legislación más dura, porque solo así derrotaremos el narcotráfico. Pero no con Gobiernos que abandonen a sus policías, sino con una Europa que les reconozca, les respalde y les proteja.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, le narcotrafic est une menace majeure pour nos sociétés. Il alimente les violences, corrompt nos économies et fragilise l’état de droit. Face à des organisations criminelles qui opèrent à l’échelle mondiale, notre réponse doit être européenne.

Mais ne nous trompons pas de combat. Le narcotrafic ne se combattra pas en entretenant la confusion entre migration et criminalité organisée. Les réseaux qui acheminent la drogue vers les ports européens n’ont rien à voir avec celles et ceux qui fuient les conflits et les persécutions. Penser qu’une politique migratoire toujours plus restrictive répondra à nos défis sécuritaires est une impasse politique et une erreur stratégique. La lutte contre le narcotrafic exige autre chose, notamment davantage de coopération entre les États membres et une action déterminée contre le blanchiment d’argent.
Soyons fermes contre les trafiquants. Soyons lucides sur les réponses à apporter. Refusons les raccourcis qui affaiblissent à la fois notre sécurité et nos valeurs.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Mesdames et Messieurs, chers collègues, face au narcotrafic, il ne faut plus des mots mais des actes, car, derrière chaque cargaison interceptée, il y a désormais du sang versé dans nos villes européennes.

L’Union européenne semble enfin prendre conscience de l’ampleur de la menace. Nous avons applaudi des deux mains un accord important avec l’Équateur – dont j’ai été le rapporteur –, pays devenu un point stratégique dans le trafic de cocaïne vers l’Europe. Nous avons également tout fait pour renforcer l’agence de police européenne Europol, afin de mieux coordonner la lutte contre les réseaux criminels transnationaux.

Autant de vraies avancées contre des narcomafias qui désormais kidnappent, corrompent, intimident et, bien souvent, tuent en plein jour. Je pense au jeune Mehdi Kessaci, au père de famille et chauffeur Uber Nessim Ramdane, à Marseille, ou encore à l’étudiante Socayna Jean, victimes des balles, des kalashnikovs, des narcotrafiquants, et tous morts à Marseille, devenue capitale française du narcotrafic. Derrière Marseille, d’autres villes suivront si rien n’est fait: Anvers, Hambourg, Rotterdam. De par mon métier de policier, j’ai vu l’organisation de ces groupes et leur force de frappe sans foi ni loi. Notre faiblesse depuis des décennies est leur principal carburant.

Pour tous ceux qui l’ont payé de leur vie: reprenons le contrôle de nos frontières maritimes, protégeons nos ports stratégiques et donnons des moyens réels à nos douaniers, policiers, gendarmes, magistrats et services de renseignement!

paragraphs.text: Écoutez, cher collègue, la corruption est un combat que nous devons tous mener, mais la majorité de nos policiers, gendarmes, agents pénitentiaires, services de renseignement et militaires font un travail exceptionnel.

Je veux le redire ici: le problème, ce n’est pas majoritairement la corruption dans nos démocraties, ce sont des voyous qu’on a laissés que trop faire et qui ont bénéficié d’un laxisme judiciaire, d’un laxisme politique, d’une lâcheté… Et en France, l’extrême gauche et la gauche sont membres des partis qui défendent des voyous, des criminels, plutôt que nos policiers, nos gendarmes.
Donc, il faut changer de logiciel et il faut une vraie révolution, avec une volonté transpartisane de lutter contre ce narcotrafic, qui peut mettre à bas nos démocraties.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Mam przekonanie, że Unia Europejska przez długi czas nie doceniała problemu ochrony granic, pozostawiając państwa na zewnętrznych granicach Unii bez dostatecznego wsparcia. Aby sprawić, że granice Unii będą bezpieczne, należy spełnić kilka warunków. Kraje graniczne muszą uzyskać znaczące wsparcie finansowe związane z zadaniami ochrony morskiej i lądowej granicy zewnętrznej. Służby krajowe muszą zostać wzmocnione i mieć stosowne narzędzia techniczne – także te, które były tu, w Parlamencie Europejskim, poddawane powszechnej krytyce. Frontex musi wszechstronnie wspierać służby krajowe, a nie prowadzić postępowania wobec funkcjonariuszy. Dość z polityczną poprawnością – państwa muszą zliberalizować przepisy dotyczące używania środków przymusu bezpośredniego, a funkcjonariuszom zapewnić bezpieczeństwo prawne.

Nie sposób nie wiązać przestępczości narkotykowej z grupami przestępczymi rekrutującymi się z obywateli państw trzecich, nielegalnych imigrantów i oszustów azylowych. Aplikujący o pobyt w Unii muszą mieć świadomość, że nieprzestrzeganie prawa wiąże się z szybką karą i skuteczną readmisją. Skuteczna ochrona granic jest pierwszym krokiem przywrócenia porządku i bezpieczeństwa w wielu miastach europejskich.

Skuteczna ochrona granic jest pierwszym krokiem przywrócenia porządku i bezpieczeństwa w wielu miastach europejskich.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, iedere dag weer gaan onze mensen van de politie en de douane de strijd aan tegen internationale drugsbendes. Door kleine ruimtes kruipend op zoek naar drugs, verstopt op de meest onwaarschijnlijke plekken, geïntimideerd door georganiseerde criminelen die ze proberen te corrumperen. Het gevecht tegen deze onterechte criminaliteit dwingt ons allemaal harder en slimmer te gaan lopen. Een paar heilige huisjes zullen omver moeten: minder nationaal denken, meer Europees.

Ten eerste, meer middelen, meer bevoegdheden en meer mogelijkheden voor Europol, onze unieke Europese politie, met meer operationele aanwezigheid in het veld en meer investeringen in innovaties zoals artificiële intelligentie en drones. Ten tweede, een ambitieuze Europese anti-corruptiestrategie. Zonder corruptie is er geen drugshandel. Ten derde, durven blijven investeren in preventie in onze wijken om te voorkomen dat kwetsbare kinderen gerekruteerd worden door drugscriminelen. Narcos is meer dan een Netflixtitel en cosmetische oplossingen krijgen van mij een duimpje omlaag.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you colleague Oliveira, yes – debates get hijacked all the time in this House by those who want to put every single fault on a single country or a single group of people. To me, it is really important to understand that drug trafficking is from all times.

Colleague Tertsch will remember that, in Spain, the country that I come from originally, we had huge problems with drug gangs in Galicia and they were all home-grown. They were not coming from outside the European Union – they were Spanish home-grown. In the Netherlands we see criminals that are international, but also home-grown, and in other countries we see the same. So it's really important that we take this as the problem that it is and not try to make it into a different problem which citizens are not particularly interested in.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, how many women have to be raped and murdered before you all start doing anything? How many children have to die at the hands of vile criminals and murderers before you realise what is happening outside? How many seniors have to become victims of those criminals in Europe before you start thinking about the future of Europe and the safety of Europeans? We just need to secure our external borders right now, immediately – we need to protect our borders at all costs.

People just deserve this safety, and we need to start with mass deportations right now. Every illegal immigrant from Europe has to be deported – even every legal immigrant who does not respect our way of life and our laws and committed a crime has to be deported. As soon as you do this, you will realise how the narco-trafficking problem, which we are discussing right now, just disappears. As soon as you do this, you will see how the numbers of rapes, violent attacks and murders just drops down.
If you are not ready to fight for Europe, then we need to replace you, defeat you in the elections and save Europe for our children.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, la recente perdita di due agenti della Guardia civile spagnola per lo speronamento da parte di una barca di narcotrafficanti è l'ennesima dimostrazione di quanto il traffico di stupefacenti costituisca una seria minaccia per le nostre società.
Come mamma di due appartenenti alle forze dell'ordine voglio esprimere la mia solidarietà alle loro famiglie.

Enormi profitti per le organizzazioni criminali, perdita di vite umane, corruzione, riciclaggio, violenza dilagante, minori reclutati, insicurezza ed enormi costi sanitari e sociali: tutto questo è ed è sempre stato il traffico di droga.

E l'impatto sull'Europa – mercato di consumo, hub di transito e luogo di produzione – è davvero enorme. Dobbiamo quindi proseguire con decisione nell'attuazione della strategia ProtectEU e soprattutto nel piano d'azione per individuare e contrastare le rotte di traffico marittime, terrestri e aeree, rafforzare la cooperazione tra Frontex, Europol, l'MAOC-N e le forze di polizia nazionali, migliorare lo scambio di informazioni tra autorità doganali di contrasto e giudiziarie e rafforzare la cooperazione con i paesi terzi di origine degli stupefacenti.

Per questo occorre dotare di risorse e di mezzi le nostre forze di polizia, ma occorre anche investire in prevenzione e recupero per contrastare non solo l'offerta, ma anche la domanda di stupefacenti.
È questa, contro la droga, una battaglia non facile, è vero, ma che l'Unione europea intera non può permettersi di perdere.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Europe's ports have become a gateway for organised crime. Record amounts of cocaine are entering the European Union, fuelling violence, corruption and criminal networks. Our law enforcement officers, custom authorities and coastguards deserve all our support. They need better tools, modern technology and stronger cooperation across Europe, not more bureaucracy.

But if we are talking about corruption, we also need to talk about protecting the workers in the ports, because we all know how much money the organised crime has, and sometimes the port workers, without protection, have to make the choice between their lives or being corrupted. So it goes hand in hand. If we talk about our law enforcement authorities, they have to have better tools, but we also need to protect the workers in the ports.

The fight against drug trafficking starts at our borders. We need stronger port security, closer cooperation between Member States and Europol, and the relentless effort to dismantle criminal networks and seize their assets. The safety of our citizens depends on it.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario, hoy no voy a hablar de lo peligrosas que son las mafias del Estrecho. Eso ya lo sabemos todos: sabemos que tienen más dinero, sabemos que, sorprendentemente, tienen más medios y sabemos que son cada vez más violentas.

Lo que no entiendo es por qué seguimos tratando a quien nos defiende como si el problema no fuera sangrante. En la frontera del sur de España, los guardias civiles mueren, señorías, mueren y no tienen reconocida la tan peleada profesión de riesgo. Todavía seguimos sin considerar eurodelito las agresiones a las fuerzas y cuerpos de seguridad europeos que se juegan la vida, cada día, frente a criminales con armas de guerra, sin seguridad física y sin seguridad jurídica.

Y todavía hay Gobiernos en los que se toman decisiones incomprensibles, como el de España, al desmantelar la unidad OCON‑Sur, una unidad que había logrado miles de detenciones y algunos de los mayores golpes al narcotráfico en el Campo de Gibraltar.

Este es el mensaje que reciben las mafias. Ellas se organizan, ellas se arman, avanzan y nosotros desmantelamos herramientas que funcionan. Señorías, despierten: la violencia extrema se combate con medios, con contundencia y con autoridad.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, κύριε Επίτροπε, σήμερα βρισκόμαστε εδώ όχι μόνο για να συζητήσουμε αλλά κυρίως για να εκφράσουμε την ευγνωμοσύνη και τον σεβασμό μας στους αφανείς ήρωες, στις γυναίκες και στους άνδρες του Πολεμικού Ναυτικού, των εθνικών ακτοφυλακών, των σωμάτων ασφαλείας, της Frontex και όλων των ευρωπαϊκών υπηρεσιών που αγωνίζονται για την καταπολέμηση της μάστιγας των ναρκωτικών· σε όλους εκείνους που με αυταπάρνηση και υψηλό αίσθημα καθήκοντος φυλάσσουν τα εθνικά και ευρωπαϊκά μας σύνορα.

Η απειλή των ναρκωτικών μπορεί πολλές φορές να μοιάζει μακρινή και αθέατη, στην πραγματικότητα όμως είναι διαρκής, οργανωμένη και αδυσώπητη. Γνωρίζουμε καλά το βαρύ αποτύπωμα στις γειτονιές, στους δρόμους και στις πόλεις μας. Γνωρίζουμε όμως εξίσου καλά ότι η καταπολέμηση των ναρκωτικών απαιτεί συνεχή επαγρύπνηση, άριστο συντονισμό και διεθνή συνεργασία. Γι' αυτό οφείλουμε από αυτή την αίθουσα να ενισχύουμε διαρκώς το έργο όσων επιχειρούν καθημερινά στις θάλασσες και στα λιμάνια της Ευρώπης, στην πρώτη γραμμή της μάχης απέναντι στο οργανωμένο έγκλημα. Κάθε φορτίο ναρκωτικών που αναχαιτίζεται δεν θα φτάσει ποτέ στις κοινωνίες μας. Και κάθε εγκληματικό δίκτυο που εξαρθρώνεται είναι μια νίκη για την ασφάλεια, την ανθρώπινη αξιοπρέπεια και τη συνοχή των κοινωνιών της Ευρώπης.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, si le narcotrafic prospère, c’est parce que – disons-le – nos frontières sont devenues des passoires et que l’Union européenne continue de multiplier les obstacles à ceux qui sont chargés de les protéger. Nos policiers, nos douaniers et nos magistrats ont besoin d’une coopération renforcée, pas d’une bureaucratie supplémentaire. Il faut faciliter la collecte et l’échange des données entre les autorités nationales, Europol, Frontex et Eurojust. Les cartels, eux, n’attendent pas les autorisations de Bruxelles pour partager leurs informations.

Pourtant, le Contrôleur européen de la protection des données a suspendu la coopération entre Europol et Frontex. C’est une décision totalement déconnectée de la réalité du terrain. À force de privilégier les contraintes administratives sur l’efficacité opérationnelle, ce sont les criminels qui en sortent gagnants.

Nous devons également clarifier le rôle de la future Agence européenne des douanes. Il n’est pas question de créer une nouvelle couche institutionnelle qui viendrait brouiller les missions d’Europol et de Frontex.

Enfin, donnons à l’Alliance des ports européens les moyens d’échanger librement leurs renseignements avec les autorités de police et de justice. Face à des mafias toujours plus puissantes, notre réponse doit être simple: plus de coopération, plus de renseignement, plus d’efficacité et moins d’idéologie.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, un vas pleacă încărcat cu 10 tone de cocaină dintr-o țară sud-americană către Europa; fiul de 16 ani al unui doctor din Bruxelles - sau din Paris, sau din Berlin, sau din Roma, sau din București - încearcă primul său gram la o petrecere. Este un copil bun, cu rezultate extraordinare la școală, bine educat de părinți și cu un viitor luminos în față - sau cel puțin așa trebuia să-i fie viitorul până la acel prim gram. Știe că nu este bun, dar prietenii râd de el că nu are curaj să încerce și își spune că este puternic și că va fi o singură dată, apoi se va opri.

În timp ce băiatul trage prima sa linie de „zăpadă” sau „pudra morții”, alt vas încărcat ajunge într-un port european și reușește să descarce marfa. Zecile de tone înseamnă sute de mii, chiar milioane de victime, de dependenți, de tineri care își anulează viitorul, de copii buni precum al meu sau ai voștri.

Și fix în timp ce se întâmplă toate astea, în Parlamentul European, unii colegi de-ai noștri votează să nu întărească structurile de forță competente în combaterea traficului de droguri. Adică fix acele structuri care ar fi putut opri cele două vase venite de pe mare și ne-ar fi putut salva copiii.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, les cartels entrent en Europe par nos failles. La ligne portée en France par Bruno Retailleau doit trouver son prolongement européen. Le narcotrafic n’est plus l’écume de faits divers dispersés, c’est une puissance criminelle, maritime, financière, territoriale. Elle défie nos États, elle jauge nos frontières, elle appelle des moyens d’exception.

Cette puissance transforme nos scrupules en couloir de circulation. Quand il faut empêcher un trafiquant identifié de revenir sur son point de deal, une partie de la gauche trouve l’État trop ferme. Quand les habitants réclament de l’air, elle rouvre le débat sur la dépénalisation. C’est une étrange boussole: moins de contraintes pour les dealers, plus d’abandon pour nos populations.

Lorsque la drogue entre par la mer, c’est l’Europe qui prend l’eau, emportée par une vague qui gagne nos campagnes, qui finit par recruter, par abîmer et par tuer nos enfants. Mais, pendant un an, Monsieur Retailleau était à Beauvau: réforme de la police judiciaire, recrutement des OPJ, paiement des heures supplémentaires, simplification de la procédure pénale, mais aussi peines planchers, peines minimales pour lutter contre les récidivistes et les délinquants qui s’en prennent à l’uniforme de la République.

Vous ne l’avez pas fait pendant un an: du courage, Céline Imart, rejoignez Marine Le Pen et Jordan Bardella! Le redressement, c’est maintenant! Ce que vous n’avez pas pu ou voulu faire, faites-le à nos côtés! Le pronostic vital de notre pays est engagé.

paragraphs.text: Merci, Monsieur Valet, pour votre très aimable invitation. Je tiens à vous rappeler que Bruno Retailleau n’était pas ministre de la justice, mais ministre de l’intérieur. Donc, il a agi sur les compétences qu’il avait à l’intérieur de son portefeuille, qui malheureusement ne concernent pas notamment la justice pour les mineurs.

Mais il a agi sur ce qui, dans son portefeuille, pouvait être fait, c’est-à-dire avoir une loi d’urgence narcotrafic, qui va aller taper les trafiquants au portefeuille, qui va mobiliser les forces de l’ordre et les rendre plus efficaces sur ces points de deal.

Je crois que nous avons des convictions assez similaires sur ce sujet, et en tout cas le combat continue à l’échelle française, mais aussi à l’échelle européenne, parce que ce combat-là, il est vital pour nos enfants.

paragraphs.text: Fru formand! Kære kollegaer. Jeg har været politibetjent i 19 år, og jeg ved, hvad narkotika i virkeligheden er. Det er at banke på en dør klokken to om natten. En far og en mor åbner, og deres ansigter krakelerer, når de forstår, hvorfor. Deres barn er død af en overdosis. Det glemmer man aldrig.

Imens så strømmer kokainen ind gennem Europas havne og grænser. Og hvad gør EU? De skriver strategier, mens narkobagmændene tjener milliarder. Strategier alene stopper ikke forbryderne. Det gør betjentene, tolderne og effektiv kontrol. Så løsningen, det er ikke mere EU. Løsningen er permanent grænse- og havnekontrol, stærke nationale politistyrker og hårdere straffe. Giv landene magten tilbage og politiet de redskaber, der skal til for at stoppe forbryderne.
Mine gamle kollegaer knokler hver evig eneste dag, så svigt dem ikke. Det skylder vi både dem og vores unge mennesker.

paragraphs.text: Next year, the 'Prüm Regulation' will enter into force for automated data exchange of DNA profiles, fingerprints and number plates of vehicles of criminals. Your country, Denmark, cannot participate in this system and will not be able to exchange data of criminals with other countries. How do you think Denmark can stay a safe country without this key instrument if it keeps the opt‑out on justice and home affairs?
