paragraphs.text: Jeg er rigtig stolt af, at vi i Danmark har vores retsforbehold, for jeg har selv arbejdet med international og grænseoverskridende kriminalitet igennem 10 år. Og vores retsforbehold i Danmark beskytter både politiet og vores lovgivning. Det beskytter således, at vi faktisk kan implementere nye efterforskningsmetoder uden at skulle spørge EU om lov. Og det gør, at man kan tilpasse efterforskningsmetoderne inden for det land, man nu kommer fra.

Så jeg er stolt af, at vi i Danmark har et retsforbehold, som beskytter os på lige præcis det her område. Og til det skal jeg også sige, at i og med at jeg selv har arbejdet inden for det her område, så har vi en lang række parallelaftaler i Danmark. Og Danmark er måske en af dem, der er mest førende og bedst til at opklare international organiseret kriminalitet. Så derfor har vi parallelaftaler, som gør, at vi kan få alle de samme oplysninger, som man sidder og forhandler om i den nye aftale.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Nie da się mówić o przestępczości zorganizowanej, która trudni się handlem narkotykami, bez tematu nielegalnej imigracji. Tak się składa, że akurat koalicja rządząca w Unii Europejskiej jest odpowiedzialna za wpuszczenie nielegalnych imigrantów. Więc jeżeli chcecie zwalczyć drogę dotyczącą narkotyków, to musicie też zająć się nielegalną imigracją. Temat, który dotyczy konsekwencji chociażby za pomoc związaną z nielegalnymi imigrantami pod przykrywką organizacji pozarządowych, leży i nie jest dalej procedowany, dlatego, że lewica to blokuje.

Może warto zwrócić uwagę na to, jakim doświadczeniem może podzielić się Polska. Tak się składa, że miałem przyjemność być w rządzie, który zatrzymał nielegalną migrację, który doprowadził do tego, że odsyłano nielegalnych migrantów.

Ale co się dzieje? Zaraz na drugi dzień przyjmujecie rozwiązania, które są związane z paktem migracyjnym. Chcecie, aby ci migranci, z których wielu trudni się działalnością przestępczą – wzrost przestępczości na różnym tle, w tym seksualnym, jest gigantyczny – zostali przerzuceni do innych krajów? Więc prosta odpowiedź jest taka: zero nielegalnych migrantów i zamkniemy również temat związany ze skalą problemu z narkotykami.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, igual les parezco un poco dura, pero voy a decir algo.
La droga que mañana van a ofrecer a cualquiera de nuestros hijos, la cocaína en cualquier capital europea, probablemente venga de España, todo un país europeo.

España es la principal puerta del sur de Europa, y es una puerta que está completamente abierta. Es la puerta por la que se está colando buena parte de la droga que está envenenando nuestro continente.

Tranquilos, porque esta frontera tiene guardianes, guardias civiles valientes que cada noche salen a plantarle cara al narco con más vocación que recursos. Pero quiero decirle algo, comisario: les estamos mandando a la guerra sin armas. Mientras enfrente tienen semisumergibles y armamento bélico, detrás tienen un Estado cada vez más débil y un Gobierno enfermo de corrupción.

Ha muerto gente en Barbate, han muerto en Huelva y van a seguir muriendo. Porque los criminales los matan, sí. Pero por falta también de nuestra voluntad política. Así que, comisario, por favor, más recursos para Europa y para Frontex, más inteligencia compartida, penas más duras contra los criminales.
No esperemos al próximo funeral para reconocer el peligro. Son una profesión de riesgo.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Tylko w 2024 roku państwa członkowskie Unii Europejskiej zgłosiły ponad półtora miliona przestępstw związanych z narkotykami. Belgijska Antwerpia jest dla gangów narkotykowych bramą przemytu do Europy – przypadkiem, tuż pod nosem eurokratów, tych nauczycieli praworządności.

W latach 2018–2023 liczba pacjentów rozpoczynających leczenie z powodu problemów związanych z kokainą wzrosła o 31%. Liczba osób rozpoczynających leczenie z powodu uzależnienia od cracku wzrosła o 35%. Taka skala przemytu narkotyków to dzieło Komisji Europejskiej. To polityka otwartych granic. W czasie, gdy Europejczycy boją się gangów narkotykowych w swoich miastach, kartele narkotykowe traktują europejskie wybrzeża i porty jak swoje magazyny. Służby ochrony granic potrzebują realnego wsparcia, twardego prawa i wolnej ręki w działaniu, a nie ataku lewicowej agendy ze strony Komisji Europejskiej.

Powiem szczerze: brak waszej skuteczności w zwalczaniu przemytu narkotyków do Europy nasuwa pytanie, czy wy czasami nie współpracujecie z przemytnikami i nie czerpiecie jakichś korzyści finansowych z handlu narkotykami w Europie. Tak dla kolegi pytam.

interventions.text: Procedura "catch-the-eye"

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário, a nova estratégia de combate às drogas da União Europeia não pode repetir dois erros: esquecer a emergência do combate às drogas sintéticas, ignorar que as suas fronteiras ocidentais começam no coração do Atlântico com os Açores e com a Madeira.

É pelo Atlântico que têm passado rotas cada vez mais exploradas por redes internacionais de tráfico de droga, com barcos, drones e até narcossubmarinos. É por isso que é urgente reforçar a vigilância marítima, a tecnologia, a partilha de informação, a cooperação para as agências europeias, mas também o reconhecimento da importância das nossas forças de segurança que tanto têm feito com tão pouco.

Precisamos também de reconhecer que as fronteiras externas da União Europeia começam pelos Açores e pela Madeira, e os Açores e a Madeira têm um papel fundamental na segurança da União Europeia. E é também por isso que precisamos de ter uma nova estratégia para o Atlântico, que enquadre as novas tensões geopolíticas, mas também o combate ao tráfico de droga e a segurança da União Europeia.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, i nostri confini sono un colabrodo e voi lo sapete.

Oggi parliamo di narcotraffico nel Mediterraneo, ma la droga è il sintomo: la malattia è che noi non difendiamo i nostri confini, perché ogni anno dai nostri porti arrivano tonnellate di droga – soprattutto dal Nord Africa – che stanno uccidendo migliaia di giovani europei.

Quella stessa rotta, che negli ultimi 15 anni ha portato clandestinamente, via mare, un milione e mezzo di immigrati in Italia e tre milioni in Europa, è stata sfruttata anche per trafficare droga e armi e alimentare profitti miliardari per le mafie.
Mentre voi predicavate porti aperti e mentre von der Leyen e le sinistre europee trasformavano Frontex in un bersaglio ideologico, scafisti e organizzazioni criminali facevano affari d'oro.
Difendere i confini non è uno slogan, è l'unico strumento serio e concreto per bloccare il narcotraffico.

Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, i nostri confini sono un colabrodo e voi lo sapete.

Oggi parliamo di narcotraffico nel Mediterraneo, ma la droga è il sintomo: la malattia è che noi non difendiamo i nostri confini, perché ogni anno dai nostri porti arrivano tonnellate di droga – soprattutto dal Nord Africa – che stanno uccidendo migliaia di giovani europei.

Quella stessa rotta, che negli ultimi 15 anni ha portato clandestinamente, via mare, un milione e mezzo di immigrati in Italia e tre milioni in Europa, è stata sfruttata anche per trafficare droga e armi e alimentare profitti miliardari per le mafie.

Mentre voi predicavate porti aperti e mentre von der Leyen e le sinistre europee trasformavano Frontex in un bersaglio ideologico, scafisti e organizzazioni criminali facevano affari d'oro.

Difendere i confini non è uno slogan, è l'unico strumento serio e concreto per bloccare il narcotraffico.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, let us be brutally blunt: Europe is losing control of its security. Open‑border policies fuel chaos, turning narco‑trafficking into a real threat for all of us. The core issue is a catastrophic failure of integration. Multigenerational migrant neighbourhoods are forming parallel societies that reject European values. In Sweden, second generation migrants dominate gangs behind record bombings. In France, suburb drug wars drive hundreds of narco‑homicides. Criminal groups exploit this isolation. They turn youth into foot soldiers and use minors as legal shields for drugs and killings. We can no longer deny the link between uncontrolled migration, failed integration and tribal gang violence. The age of naive multiculturalism must be over.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário Costas Kadis, é preciso atuar em duas dimensões: por um lado, combater a toxicodependência, fazendo desaparecer o negócio lucrativo do narcotráfico; por outro lado, combater o tráfico de droga e as redes criminosas que nele florescem.

Em ambas as dimensões, o papel dos Estados é determinante. Para vencer este combate, precisamos de políticas eficazes de combate à toxicodependência, serviços públicos de saúde e inserção social robustos, de investimento público no tratamento e reabilitação dos consumidores.

Precisamos também de medidas de política criminal adequadas e de investimento nas forças e serviços de segurança nacionais, incluindo nas alfândegas, melhorando as condições de trabalho dos seus profissionais e reforçando a sua capacidade operacional.
Ao mesmo tempo, precisamos de nos libertar das imposições da UE sobre os orçamentos nacionais que condicionam o investimento público, que é essencial para todos estes objetivos.

E não podemos permitir que o combate ao narcotráfico seja o pretexto para a militarização, para justificar medidas de vigilância indiscriminada sobre os cidadãos, ou para propagandear suspeitas e preconceitos de natureza racista e xenófoba, como infelizmente acabámos de ouvir nas últimas intervenções feitas pela extrema‑direita.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, le trafic de drogue obéit aux lois classiques de l’offre et de la demande. Aussi, tant qu’il y aura des consommateurs, il y aura des trafiquants de drogue, et le trafic de drogue continuera avec son cortège de morts, de destruction de la santé d’une partie de nos populations et de déstabilisation de nos sociétés.

Si nous voulons triompher dans cette lutte contre le trafic de drogue, alors nous devons travailler à dissuader la consommation de drogue. Cela passera par trois stratégies. Premièrement, le déploiement de sanctions dissuasives contre les consommateurs de drogue. Deuxièmement, la diffusion massive, dans tous les médias, de spots d’information sur les ravages de la drogue sur la santé, mais également sur les morts occasionnées, car les consommateurs doivent prendre conscience du fait qu’ils ont du sang sur les mains. Dernier point, la confiscation systématique de tous les biens acquis grâce au trafic de drogue. C’est ainsi que nous triompherons.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, «hay noches en que estamos solos mi compañero y yo contra quince narcolanchas». Desgraciadamente, no es el comienzo de una serie colombiana de Netflix: se trata del testimonio de un guardia civil español, denunciando la indefensión con la que nuestros agentes se ven obligados a combatir al narco.

Una indefensión que tiene un altísimo coste humano. En los últimos dos años, cuatro agentes han sido asesinados en España y, en las últimas semanas, uno en Portugal. Esta escalada de violencia más propia de otras latitudes es la nueva normalidad en las costas europeas, pero Europa no puede seguir tolerándolo.

No podemos seguir dependiendo del heroísmo de nuestros agentes. Los Gobiernos europeos tienen la obligación —política y moral— de dotarles de los mejores medios para combatir al narco. Ellos no quieren palmaditas en la espalda ni homenajes en los funerales, aunque algunos ni siquiera se atrevan a hacerlo, quieren simplemente los medios para poder cumplir con su deber en defensa de todos los europeos.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, thank you for your remarks. We have taken good note of all your positions. I will make some general comments.

I think that we all agree that no Member State can face security challenges alone. We are bringing the full weight of EU legal, financial and operational resources to support Member States in this fight. We have agreed on a new EU drugs strategy, an action plan against drugs trafficking, and we are already working on their implementation. We have proposed new mandates for Europol and Eurojust, and we will propose new legislation on Frontex and organised crime soon. So in all these initiatives, we count on your cooperation and support to make real progress.

paragraphs.text: Joachim Stanisław Brudziński (ECR), na piśmieJeśli handel narkotykami kwitnie, to dlatego, że ochrona granic zewnętrznych pozostaje niewystarczająca. Państwa graniczne potrzebują większego wsparcia finansowego, nowoczesnych narzędzi i silniejszej współpracy z Frontexem, Europolem oraz Eurojustem. Zamiast mnożyć biurokrację i ograniczać wymianę informacji między służbami, Unia Europejska powinna zapewnić im skuteczne instrumenty działania. Nie ma również potrzeby tworzenia kolejnych instytucji, jeśli osłabią one kompetencje istniejących agencji.W 2024 roku państwa członkowskie Unii Europejskiej zgłosiły ponad 1,5 miliona przestępstw związanych z narkotykami. W latach 2018–2023 liczba osób rozpoczynających leczenie z powodu problemów z kokainą wzrosła o 31%, a z powodu uzależnienia od cracku o 35%. To pokazuje, że Europa przegrywa walkę z przemytem narkotyków i zorganizowaną przestępczością.Przestępcy nie mogą czuć się bezkarnie. Europejskie porty nie mogą być magazynami i punktami prze0ładunkowymi dla karteli narkotykowych. Wiele danych wskazuje na związek między przestępczością narkotykową a nielegalną migracją oraz nadużywaniem procedur azylowych. Osoby łamiące prawo powinny mieć pełną świadomość, że łamanie prawa będzie skutkowało szybkim powrotem do kraju pochodzenia.Europa potrzebuje bezpiecznych granic zamiast ideologii, współpracujących służb zamiast przepisów, które uniemożliwiają im skuteczne działanie, realnej ochrony granic i zdecydowanych działań przeciwko międzynarodowym kartelom, aby przywrócić bezpieczeństwo swoim obywatelom.

paragraphs.text: Cienītā sēdes vadītāja! Kolēģi! Krievijas pilna mēroga uzbrukums Ukrainai, kas turpinās nu jau piekto gadu, nav tikai militārs konflikts. Krievijas neoimperiālistiskai agresijai ir un būs dziļa un ilgstoša ietekme uz starptautiskajām tiesībām, Eiropas drošību, demokrātiju un miljoniem cilvēku dzīvi. Visi Krievijas valsts instrumenti – valdība, ekonomika, finanšu sektors, propaganda, pareizticīgā baznīca – kalpo karam un militarizē sabiedrību. Tāpēc vienīgais ceļš uz Krievijas atdzimšanu un sabiedrības atveseļošanu ir Ukrainas uzvara karā. Krievijas neoimperiālisms ir jāaptur. Tikai caur sakāvi Krievija var kļūt par valsti, kurā attīstīsies demokrātija, valdīs likuma vara, būs nodrošinātas cilvēktiesības un pamatbrīvības. Tāpēc mūsu pienākums ir atbalstīt Ukrainas pašaizsardzību. Eiropas Parlaments ir demokrātijas mājvieta. Tāpēc mēs atbalstām Krievijas demokrātisko opozīciju, pilsonisko sabiedrību, cilvēktiesību aktīvistus, kuri nosoda agresiju pret Ukrainu. Viņi turpina pretestību Kremļa režīmam, neskatoties uz represijām, apcietināšanām un trimdu. Režīms nežēlīgi vēršas pret katru, kas neatbalsta agresiju. Ir ierosinātas vairāk nekā 5000 krimināllietas, cietumos smok vairāk nekā 4000 politieslodzīto. Politieslodzīto atbrīvošana ir prasība, kura ir jāiekļauj Ukrainas un Krievijas miera sarunās, kuras agrāk vai vēlāk notiks. Tomēr Krievijas demokrātiskie spēki ir sašķelti. Vēsture atkal un atkal ir pierādījusi, ka diktatūru uzvar tie, kas uzvaras vārdā atliek malā uzskatu un personāliju nesaskaņas un koncentrējas uz stratēģisko mērķi – demokrātiskas un likumpaklausīgas valsts un sabiedrības izveidošanu. Bez vienotības Krievijas demokrātisko spēku ietekme uz politisko procesu Krievijā būs maznozīmīga.

Tāpēc mēs atbalstām Krievijas demokrātisko opozīciju, pilsonisko sabiedrību, cilvēktiesību aktīvistus, kuri nosoda agresiju pret Ukrainu. Viņi turpina pretestību Kremļa režīmam, neskatoties uz represijām, apcietināšanām un trimdu. Režīms nežēlīgi vēršas pret katru, kas neatbalsta agresiju. Ir ierosinātas vairāk nekā 5000 krimināllietas, cietumos smok vairāk nekā 4000 politieslodzīto. Politieslodzīto atbrīvošana ir prasība, kura ir jāiekļauj Ukrainas un Krievijas miera sarunās, kuras agrāk vai vēlāk notiks. Tomēr Krievijas demokrātiskie spēki ir sašķelti. Vēsture atkal un atkal ir pierādījusi, ka diktatūru uzvar tie, kas uzvaras vārdā atliek malā uzskatu un personāliju nesaskaņas un koncentrējas uz stratēģisko mērķi – demokrātiskas un likumpaklausīgas valsts un sabiedrības izveidošanu. Bez vienotības Krievijas demokrātisko spēku ietekme uz politisko procesu Krievijā būs maznozīmīga.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Alessandra Moretti, a nome del gruppo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la Russia non è Putin.

La Russia sono anche migliaia di donne e uomini che, in un clima asfissiante, continuano a difendere la democrazia, i diritti umani e le libertà fondamentali. Sono persone che si oppongono alla brutale guerra di aggressione della Russia contro l'Ucraina ed è proprio da loro che ogni giorno ci arrivano innumerevoli segnalazioni di cittadini repressi, detenuti, imprigionati e maltrattati solo perché si sono esposti, hanno alzato la testa e la voce dicendo la verità sulla guerra di Putin.

La propaganda del regime impedisce alle forze democratiche di esprimersi e quando qualcuno riesce a sfuggire alle maglie fittissime di questa rete, il sistema giudiziario prende la scena, confezionando sentenze ad hoc per punire attivisti, giornalisti e chiunque abbia il coraggio di alzare la voce.

L'Unione europea deve essere ferma e decisa nel suo incrollabile sostegno al popolo ucraino di fronte alla guerra di aggressione di Putin. Allo stesso tempo, l'Unione deve continuare a sostenere gli attivisti russi per i diritti umani, gli attori pro‑democrazia e gli attivisti contro la guerra, persone che spesso rischiano la propria incolumità e la propria vita per il loro impegno e per presentare un'altra Russia: la Russia libera, democratica, una Russia dello Stato di diritto. Una Russia così – ricordiamoci – è possibile.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: António Tânger Corrêa, em nome do Grupo PfE.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Caros Colegas, meus caros amigos, façamos um pouco de História.

Erros europeus desde o fim da Guerra Fria, a queda do Muro de Berlim: muito pouco diálogo político com a Rússia e total dependência energética desse país. O resultado era previsível porque nos afastámos politicamente e abraçámos uma dependência económica e energética.

Meus caros amigos, longe, muito longe de aceitar este regime na Rússia, pelo contrário, criticá-lo vivamente. Agora, nós não temos de nos imiscuir nos assuntos internos de outros países, de países terceiros, ainda por cima alheios à União Europeia.

A prioridade deve ser fixar e resolver os problemas da Europa, antes de arranjar agendas externas que nem sempre são claras nem honestas. Portanto, vamos tentar, mais uma vez, que a Europa se comporte à altura e que resolva os seus problemas em vez de andar a tentar resolver os dos outros.

interventions.speaker_label: Mariusz Kamiński, w imieniu grupy ECR.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Cieszę się, że rozmawiamy w Parlamencie Europejskim o innej Rosji, o Rosji, która nie będzie śmiertelnym zagrożeniem dla wolnego świata i która nie będzie ociekała krwią niewinnych ofiar. Czy taka Rosja jest możliwa? Kiedy spojrzymy na historię tego kraju, to trudno znaleźć podstawę do optymizmu. Zarówno carska Rosja, jak i czerwona Rosja były agresywnymi państwami imperialistycznymi. Putin czerpie z obu tych tradycji. Takie wartości jak demokracja, prawa człowieka, prawa obywatelskie w Rosji nigdy się nie zakorzeniły.

Ci, którzy marzą o tym, aby z Rosji uczynić państwo cywilizowane, są po prostu mordowani. Tak stało się z Anną Politkowską, Borysem Niemcowem, Aleksiejem Nawalnym. Dziś w Rosji nie ma żadnej zorganizowanej opozycji. Nie oznacza to, że nie należy wspierać tych, którzy, będąc w większości na emigracji, deklarują niechęć wobec dyktatury. Wsparcie to musi być jednak adekwatne do realnie podejmowanych działań oraz rzeczywiście wyznawanych wartości. Należy również pamiętać, że niemal 20% obywateli współczesnej Rosji to przedstawiciele mniejszości narodowych. Ich aspiracje narodowe zasługują na szczególną uwagę.

interventions.speaker_label: Bernard Guetta, au nom du groupe Renew.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, la géographie nous l’impose: parce que la Russie est européenne et que c’est avec elle que nous partageons ce continent, il nous faut trouver les voies et moyens de coexister dans une paix solide et durable.

Cela demande deux choses: la première est de toujours plus aider l’Ukraine à infliger à Vladimir Poutine la défaite qu’il mérite. La stabilité de notre continent exige que plus personne ne puisse croire, en Russie, que la force brutale puisse triompher du droit et que les missiles puissent reconstituer l’empire des tsars. Peut-être ce jour est-il plus proche qu’on ne le croit – on verra –, mais la certitude est que rien ne sourit plus à Vladimir Poutine, qu’aucune dictature ne survit à l’humiliation d’une déroute militaire, et qu’une page se tournera donc bientôt à Moscou, dans trois jours, trois mois ou trois ans.

Ce jour-là, nous devons le préparer, et c’est pour cela que nous avons entamé et que nous poursuivrons un dialogue avec l’opposition russe. Avant même que la victoire de l’Ukraine ne lève un vent de liberté à Moscou, il faut que les Russes – non pas le Kremlin, mais les Russes – nous entendent leur dire que nous ne voulons rien d’autre que vivre à leurs côtés, dans la sécurité et la coopération, et que, le jour venu, nous tendrons la main à une Russie libérée, enfin libre de choisir l’Europe et la démocratie.

interventions.speaker_label: Sergey Lagodinsky, on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, for too long, the EU's Russia policy has been reactive: sanctions after aggression, statements after repression, emergency support after arrests. This is not enough. This is not strategic. We need a real EU strategy on Russia with two pillars: deterrence against the current regime and the 'de-Putinisation' of the Russia of the future. This should be a European security objective.

The Brussels Dialogue conference last month showed that this is possible. For the first time, officially, the European Parliament, with support of Commission and EEAS, brought together Russian democratic forces in a structured dialogue with the EU institutions, including voices from Russia, following the initiative of Mr Kubilius a couple of years ago. The presence of Commissioner Kubilius, but also of Commissioner Marta Kos, was also important because enlargement also includes a wider strategic neighbourhood. This dialogue should mark the beginning of a more structured and political engagement with Russians who fight against Putin's regime. A Russia that remains imperialist remains a threat to Ukraine and to all of us. Europe cannot impose democracy on Russia, but we can support those Russians who fight for it, who die for it.

That is why in the next MFF we need a dedicated Global Europe funding line for Russian civil society. I call on the Commission and the Council to work on an update of the EU strategy on Russia. Stop treating Russian civil society as a side issue. They are our allies. They are our best, important weapon against Putin and for Ukraine. And this Parliament will do our best to support them and all of us.

interventions.speaker_label: Li Andersson, on behalf of The Left Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of The Left Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, missiles and drones are killing people in Kyiv every night at the moment. Putin has shown that he is a modern‑day fascist leader by trying to conquer Ukraine militarily, but also by attacking those in his own country who oppose his imperialist ideology and who do not fit into his patriarchal and heteronormative notion of the nation. It is not only our moral obligation, but also in our own interest to support the Ukrainians that are fighting for independence and are fighting against Putin's authoritarianism.

Likewise, it is also in our own interest to support those democratic Russian opposition forces who share these objectives. This means engaging in dialogue but also recognising the diversity of actors in Russian civil society, including those representing linguistic and ethnic minorities. This means supporting independent media projects and also providing refuge in Europe for those who really need it, not sending back people belonging to the LGBTQI community or those that are resisting Putin and resisting his war on Ukraine.

interventions.speaker_label: Петър Волгин, от името на групата ESN.

paragraphs.text: Господин Председател, мечтата на колективния Запад винаги е била да види Майдан в Москва. В продължение на десетилетия Западът обучаваше и финансираше много хора и организации в Русия, надявайки се те да се превърнат в неговата пета колона и сами да съсипят страната си. Но въпреки милиардите долари и евро, дадени за тази цел, мнозинството от руските граждани отхвърли данайския дар на западните лицемери. Нормалните руски граждани отлично разбират, че тези хора, въпреки всичките си високопарни слова пет пари не дават за демокрацията, свободата и просперитета на Русия. Единственото, което искат, е тотален контрол върху Руската федерация и да я грабят безнаказано.

Западът много иска да се повтори ситуацията от 90-те години, когато техният любимец Елцин и приближените му олигарси изпълняваха безпрекословно желанията на чуждите властови центрове и разпродаваха страната си. Днешното ръководство на Русия отдавна отхвърли тази васална зависимост и затова Брюксел и Вашингтон правят всичко възможно, за да го свалят. Само че нито излетите колосални суми, нито истеричната пропаганда постигнаха тази цел. Чуждестранните агенти на влияние в Русия или избягаха при своите покровители, или замълчаха засрамени.

Тотално сбъркана е политиката на колективния Запад по отношение на Русия. Вместо да водят откровен диалог с Москва, западните ръководители решиха, че могат лесно да съсипят тази държава. Сметнаха, че на безценица ще си купят руския елит така, както са правели западните колонизатори с местното население в Африка и Америка. Повярваха, че днес тлъстите грантове и безплатните воаяжи до Брюксел и Вашингтон за руснаците ще бъдат това, което някога са били искрящите мъниста за американските и африканските племенни вождове.

Да, отделни НПО-та и политици се продадоха, но в крайна сметка се оказа, че огромният финансов ресурс, отделен за антируска пропаганда, не е довел до нищо. Продължаването на тази стратегия ще доведе до същия нулев резултат.

interventions.speaker_label: Hadja Lahbib, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, the Ebola outbreak continues to expand rapidly in a region marked by conflict, displacement and fragile health systems. It is a crisis within a crisis and a reminder that, in today's interconnected world, no country can face a major health threat alone. Sustained financing and global coordination are essential.

According to the European Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, ECDC, the risk of infection for people living in the EU remains very low. But this is no reason for complacency. We remain vigilant and the Health Security Committee issued an opinion on the current recommendations for a common EU approach. The EU and our Member States are prepared for an imported Ebola case, as France's rapid response has shown.

A few weeks ago, I travelled to Bunia, in Ituri, the epicentre of the outbreak, to show EU solidarity and reaffirm our support. I saw the extraordinary bravery of healthcare and humanitarian workers operating in extremely difficult conditions. But I also saw that Europe's support matters. Our presence, our reliability and our ability to act quickly are recognised and highly valued by all partners. And our assistance is saving lives.

Major challenges remain. Our priority is to boost surveillance and contact tracing, deploy diagnostics and medical teams, support exit screening, keep humanitarian health access open, strengthen community trust, and ensure respect for international humanitarian law.

Since day one, we have worked with the WHO, the Africa CDC, affected countries and partners. ECDC experts have been deployed through the EU Health Task Force to support Africa CDC and strengthen exit screening. Overall, the EU is providing immediate and long-term support of EUR 493 million for humanitarian aid, vaccines, treatments and health security in the region. This includes more than EUR 1 million for the current preparedness and response effort, with EUR 16.5 million to rapidly deploy diagnostics and strengthen field testing capacities. We have invested EUR 39.3 million in CEPI, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, to support the development of new, broadly protective filovirus vaccines.

We have also mobilised EUR 15 million in humanitarian assistance for WHO and frontline humanitarian partners and transported more than 590 tonnes of essential supplies to eastern DRC through eight EU humanitarian air bridges.

Our response builds on years of EU investments in health security in Africa, healthcare workforce training, public health institutes and laboratory capacities, clinical trials, infrastructure, surveillance, logistics and research into vaccine therapeutics and diagnostics.

Beyond our bilateral and Team Europe action, we continue to provide significant multilateral contributions to the global health initiatives such as the Pandemic Fund, Gavi and the Global Fund, which are mobilising flexible funding to help countries respond to Ebola and maintain essential health services.

Honourable Members, while responding to the immediate crisis, we must also continue building long-term preparedness and response capacity. This is the aim of the global health resilience initiative to help countries prevent, prepare for and respond to current and future outbreaks. Containing Ebola requires solidarity, political commitment to bring a lasting solution to the conflict, sustained financing, and reliable access to lifesaving humanitarian supplies and medical equipment. I have pleaded for that already in February during my first visit to the Great Lakes region.

We must invest in what is needed today while preparing for tomorrow. This is why sustainable financing and health preparedness must go hand in hand in the next multiannual financial framework. You can count on me and my commitment to support the response, mobilise resources and advocate for humanitarian access and respect for humanitarian international law.

interventions.speaker_label: Tomislav Sokol, u ime kluba PPE.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, izbijanje ebole u Demokratskoj Republici Kongu i Ugandi ponovno nas podsjeća da zarazne bolesti ne poznaju granice.

U današnjem međusobno povezanom svijetu, zdravstvena kriza u jednom dijelu svijeta može vrlo brzo postati sigurnosni izazov i za Europu. Zato odgovor na ovakve epidemije nije samo pitanje humanitarne pomoći, nego i pitanje zdravstvene sigurnosti, otpornosti naših sustava i odgovorne međunarodne suradnje. Svjetska zdravstvena organizacija ovu je epidemiju proglasila međunarodnom javnozdravstvenom krizom. Upravo zato brzina reakcije, međunarodna koordinacija i razmjena stručnog znanja mogu biti presudni za zaustavljanje širenja bolesti.

Europska unija već je pokazala solidarnost pružanjem financijske pomoći, slanjem stručne potpore te ulaganjem u istraživanje i razvoj novih cjepiva, dijagnostike i terapije. Istodobno, EU pomaže u jačanju epidemiološkog nadzora, laboratorijskih kapaciteta i pripravnosti susjednih država kako bi se spriječilo daljnje širenje zaraze. Europa mora nastaviti pažljivo pratiti razvoj situacije. Iako stručne procjene pokazuju da je rizik za građane Europske unije trenutačno vrlo nizak, iskustva iz proteklih godina pokazala su koliko se zdravstvene okolnosti mogu brzo promijeniti. Zato moramo nastaviti ulagati u pripravnost naših zdravstvenih sustava, jačati sustave ranog upozoravanja, razvijati zajedničke europske kapacitete za odgovor na zdravstvene krize te produbljivati suradnju sa Svjetskom zdravstvenom organizacijom.

Borba protiv zaraznih bolesti test je naše sposobnosti da djelujemo zajednički, pravodobno i solidarno. Samo suradnjom, ulaganjem u znanost i odgovornim međunarodnim djelovanjem možemo spriječiti da lokalna epidemija preraste u globalnu prijetnju.
Upravo zato europska solidarnost i pripravnost moraju ostati temelj našeg odgovora na ovakve zdravstvene izazove.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Leire Pajín, en nombre del Grupo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, el brote que tiene origen en la República Democrática del Congo y en Uganda no es un asunto africano. Es un asunto global y también europeo.

Las enfermedades no se detienen en las fronteras. Un brote puede empezar muy lejos de Europa, pero tarda en llegar exactamente lo mismo que tarda en desplazarse una persona. Al principio, nos llegan noticias, cifras, unos cientos de casos y las primeras muertes —ya llevamos 500—. Entonces, podemos caer en el error de decir que, como es en África y no aquí, no es nuestro problema.

¿Alguien se acuerda de la pandemia? Porque es exactamente esto. Y yo sé que el ébola no es el COVID-19, pero deberíamos haber aprendido de la pandemia. Es absolutamente importante que nuestra respuesta sea doble. Por un lado, apoyo firme a los países afectados, prevención, preparación y respuesta desde la Unión Europea. Por otro lado, que nuestros mecanismos se compartan también en coordinación con los países del Sur Global.

Señora comisaria, yo le quiero dar las gracias por su compromiso, por ir al terreno, por su constante trabajo, por ser luz en un momento oscuro; porque necesitamos reforzar la vigilancia, la logística, la comunicación comunitaria, y la coordinación entre nuestros centros de vigilancia y los africanos. Y, sobre todo, porque la solidaridad no es caridad, es contener el brote en origen. Y es justicia. Pero es también la forma más inteligente de asegurar la seguridad de los europeos.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Thierry Mariani, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, en République démocratique du Congo, les populations subissent déjà les ravages de la guerre. Désormais, elles doivent affronter une nouvelle catastrophe: Ebola – plus de 1 500 cas, plus de 500 morts.

Mais il faut dire les choses: ce virus se propage aussi parce qu’il arrive dans des régions, l’Ituri et le Kivu, détruites par la guerre. Depuis 2021, l’est du Congo est à nouveau ravagé par les attaques du M23, soutenu par le régime de Paul Kagame. Des millions de personnes ont dû fuir, des infrastructures et des hôpitaux ont été incendiés.

Alors, comment arrêter Ebola? Comment arrêter quand il n’y a pas assez d’ambulances, quand les centres de soins sont détruits, quand les médecins ne peuvent même plus atteindre les malades? Oui, il faut envoyer de l’aide humanitaire, mais fermer les yeux sur les vrais responsables de ce chaos, c’est accepter que la situation continue; c’est nous rendre complices.

L’Union européenne doit enfin agir, comme le demande le Parlement depuis plusieurs années: sanctionner le Rwanda et M. Kagame et faire pression pour mettre fin à cette guerre. Pourquoi tant de complaisance pour le Rwanda? C’est le moment de montrer qu’on sait faire aussi une action politique, et pas uniquement une action humanitaire!

interventions.speaker_label: Hilde Vautmans, au nom du groupe Renew.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, l’épidémie d’Ebola en RDC est une des plus graves de l’histoire. De plus, le conflit armé dans l’est de la RDC rend la lutte presque impossible. Sans sécurité, il est impossible de stopper l’épidémie.

L’Afrique, chers collègues, est un partenaire essentiel. C’est notre voisin. Face à un virus qui menace toute une région, nous ne pouvons pas rester spectateurs: nous devons protéger les civils, protéger le personnel de santé et garantir un accès à l’aide humanitaire. Et nous devons renforcer notre soutien aux organisations locales, comme l’hôpital de Panzi du Dr Denis Mukwege, qui sont en première ligne dans la lutte contre Ebola.

Nous devons aussi rétablir la sécurité dans la région. Comme d’autres intervenants l’ont dit, nous devons commencer à sanctionner le Rwanda. La paix doit revenir là-bas pour permettre le combat contre Ebola. Notre devoir est clair: sauver les vies. Chaque jour compte.

interventions.speaker_label: Ignazio Roberto Marino, a nome del gruppo Verts/ALE.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, questo virus, che in molti abbiamo paragonato a quanto è accaduto qualche anno fa con il COVID, è un virus molto più letale, molto più pericoloso: non esistono cure, non esistono vaccini e non esiste nessun modo per fermare le emorragie all'interno del corpo e all'esterno del corpo di questi poveri pazienti.

Noi dobbiamo veramente sostituirci a quanto gli Stati Uniti hanno fatto con il loro passo indietro rispetto all'Organizzazione mondiale della sanità. Se non lo vogliamo fare perché crediamo che l'aiuto e la solidarietà siano importanti, dovremmo farlo per egoismo, perché, come tanti hanno detto, a partire anche dalla Commissaria, i virus non hanno bisogno di un passaporto per attraversare un confine.

Il fatto che ci siano già stati 1 500 contagi, 500 persone che hanno perso la vita e vedere quelle immagini – dove, signora Commissaria, è vero che è stato fatto uno sforzo, ma, di fatto, sul territorio, dove queste persone muoiono, non hanno neanche la possibilità di avere quegli strumenti di protezione per i medici e per gli infermieri, tant'è vero che ne sono morti quasi venti – e anche per le stesse persone che assistono o vanno a trovare i loro cari.
Dobbiamo fare di più e dobbiamo farlo adesso, perché questo virus è veramente pericoloso e mortale.

interventions.speaker_label: Catarina Martins, em nome do Grupo The Left.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: em nome do Grupo The Left

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, bem sei que supervisionou pessoalmente o embarque de paracetamol para o Congo para ajudar no combate ao surto de Ébola. Mas é poucochinho, não é?
Queria fazer-lhe duas perguntas sobre ações concretas da União Europeia.

Em primeiro lugar, estamos perante uma variante para a qual não há nenhuma vacina comercial, mas sabemos agora que há avanços científicos que entusiasmam. E a minha pergunta é se a União Europeia vai, então, investir nestes avanços científicos para termos a vacina.

A segunda questão é sobre os serviços de saúde locais. Os Médicos Sem Fronteiras têm dito, e muito bem, que é preciso investir diretamente lá. Têm, aliás, pedido investimento direto para que os serviços de saúde possam não só monitorizar como controlar, tratar a doença. E a minha pergunta é se a União Europeia vai aumentar o seu apoio, porque tem de o fazer. Os casos detetados em Paris e Berlim mostram, aliás, que é do seu próprio interesse fazê-lo.

E uma nota final: a União Europeia tem particulares responsabilidades, porque se nas zonas de conflito é mais difícil controlar o surto de Ébola, não esqueçamos que somos parceiros comerciais daqueles minerais do sangue que estão a provocar os conflitos nas zonas mais afetadas.

Têm, aliás, pedido investimento direto para que os serviços de saúde possam não só monitorizar como controlar, tratar a doença. E a minha pergunta é se a União Europeia vai aumentar o seu apoio, porque tem de o fazer. Os casos detetados em Paris e Berlim mostram, aliás, que é do seu próprio interesse fazê-lo.

E uma nota final: a União Europeia tem particulares responsabilidades, porque se nas zonas de conflito é mais difícil controlar o surto de Ébola, não esqueçamos que somos parceiros comerciais daqueles minerais do sangue que estão a provocar os conflitos nas zonas mais afetadas.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, thank you all for this first exchange.

I totally agree that the Ebola outbreak is not an African problem. It's about all of us, because no one of us is in security until everyone is in security. We live on the same planet. So we have to acknowledge and to remind us that a virus does not need a visa to cross borders.

When it comes to investments in vaccines, the Commission is currently replenishing its rescEU stockpiles for a range of relevant medical countermeasures in Europe, also for remdesivir, an antiviral authorised in the EU against COVID-19, but which is considered and recommended by WHO as potential therapeutics against Ebola. Together with Member States, we are looking into the possibility of rolling out clinical trials with potential therapeutic candidates.

The European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership is supporting the development of monoclonal antibodies against Ebola and other filoviruses with EUR 3.4 million. And the Commission has invested over the past years heavily into the development of vaccines and therapeutics for filoviruses like Ebola and Marburg. I have to say that this Ebola Bundibugyo was already a priority. We already acknowledged that it was a threat coming soon.

Last month we launched also a call for tenders with EUR 16 million to establish an investigational vaccine reserve for human pathogenic filoviruses for which no authorised vaccines are currently available addressing Marburg, Sudan, Ebola but also Bundibugyo viruses.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, colleagues, it is again an outbreak of terrible sickness. We have Ebola in many parts of Africa, even one case on European soil. We have seen the hantavirus spreading over springtime.

I want to emphasise one important point, because this is the very beginning of one or the other sickness, and we do not know where it will lead in either case. But I have already observed extremists claiming that the sickness does not exist, that the sickness has been made up by what they call 'elites'. But these extremists are the ones who define themselves whom they call 'elites', and they create the conspiracy theory that the 'elites' would create information about the sickness to control people.

No – this is academic research, this is scientific data that what we are doing is based on. This is why, especially the European role with our approach of human dignity, of individual freedom, is to take it seriously when such outbreaks take place and to always rely on evidence, academic evidence, and to confront extremists in the very beginning when they start their conspiracy theories.

Of course pandemics and epidemic threats are ongoing, we have no chance to deny it, but in opposite, we have fragile and shrinking global health financing and global health support.

Now when we are discussing about financing and our global health, how much money we can put in, we see that we are also reducing financial capacities. Humanitarian aid and cross-border preparedness require a lot of financial means and, of course, all means which can help us.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, l’épidémie d’Ebola qui sévit en République démocratique du Congo et en Ouganda est avant tout une tragédie humanitaire. Plus de 1 700 personnes ont été infectées, et des centaines ont perdu la vie. Derrière ces chiffres se cachent des familles, des communautés et des professionnels de santé, qui luttent pour survivre dans ces circonstances difficiles.

Le contexte d’insécurité et de tensions régionales rend la situation bien plus complexe dans l’est de la RDC. Le conflit est en cours, et l’instabilité liée à la crise entre la RDC et le Rwanda complique l’accès des travailleurs humanitaires, perturbe fortement les services de santé et accentue les mouvements de population à travers les frontières.

J’appelle la Commission et le Conseil à compléter notre aide humanitaire par un engagement diplomatique renouvelé, en exhortant toutes les parties à mettre en œuvre un cessez-le-feu immédiat afin de garantir l’accès humanitaire et de protéger les civils. Car protéger des vies nécessite non seulement une aide médicale, mais aussi la paix et la stabilité, pour que les communautés puissent se rétablir.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, les nouvelles sur Ebola sont horribles, évidemment. C’est une maladie qui tue, qui fait peur aussi – transmissible, très mortelle –, mais, en même temps, il faut aussi qu’on ose s’attaquer aux causes fondamentales du problème.

En République démocratique du Congo, qu’est-ce qu’il faudrait pour combattre de manière efficace Ebola? Il ne s’agit pas uniquement de recherche d’un vaccin; il s’agit aussi d’un système de santé publique performant, de prévention – la détection! –, de pouvoir aller chercher, de pouvoir avoir les pratiques au niveau des enterrements, aussi, travailler avec les communautés locales.

Mais, pour tout cela, il faut des moyens. Et ces moyens-là, ils manquent, ils font défaut. Pourquoi? D’un côté, effectivement, parce qu’il y a tout simplement la guerre avec des acteurs impliqués comme le Rwanda, que nous sponsorisons toujours. Mais, deuxièmement, aussi à cause du pillage des ressources naturelles, organisé par les États-Unis et les multinationales européennes.

La RDC perd des sous, perd de l’argent, perd de la richesse à l’Occident et n’a donc plus les moyens pour investir dans ce système de santé publique. Donc, c’est sur cela qu’il faut travailler: sur notre politique commerciale, contre les multinationales occidentales européennes qui pillent les richesses du Congo.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, sinds 2019 weten we helaas meer dan ooit dat virussen geen grenzen kennen. Hoewel de risico's voor Europa momenteel zeer laag zijn, zien we dat de humanitaire tragedie in Congo en Oeganda vandaag nog niet volledig ingedekt is. Gelukkig kan er gerekend worden op een sterke interventie van de Wereldgezondheidsorganisatie, van de Europese Unie en van haar lidstaten, met lokale ondersteuning van de gezondheidszorg en investeringen en onderzoek naar vaccins en behandelingen, versterken we ook de globale en dus ook de eigen weerbaarheid hier bij ons tegen nieuwe varianten, zoals dat hier het geval is.

Door samen te werken, onze Afrikaanse partners te ondersteunen en te investeren in innovatie, redden we niet alleen levens ter plaatse, maar versterken we ook de gezondheid en de veiligheid van onze eigen burgers. En net dat toont aan dat er meer dan ooit nood is aan een sterke Europese gezondheidsunie. Iets waar ik ook binnen de biotechverordening naar streef. We kunnen niet wegkijken van dergelijke tragedies, dus blijft een sterke steun vanuit Europa meer dan ooit noodzakelijk. En daarvoor rekenen we op u.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, er zijn meer dan 1 500 bevestigde gevallen van ebola in Congo en Oeganda; meer dan 500 doden. Een uitbraak die zich uitbreidt naar nieuwe gebieden. Wat zo pijnlijk is, is dat we dit hebben zien aankomen: mondiale bezuinigingen op ontwikkelingssamenwerking, het afbreken van USAID. We wisten dat de crises hierdoor zouden toenemen, juist in landen waar conflicten en rampen al groot zijn. Meer geld naar infrastructuur, meer geld naar de winning van kritieke grondstoffen en minder geld naar armoedebestrijding, gezondheidszorg, onderwijs, minder geld naar de weerbaarheid van gemeenschappen. En dit is het directe gevolg.

De consequenties zijn desastreus, niet alleen voor de mensen die nu ziek zijn en die risico's lopen. Ebola ondermijnt de weg naar stabiliteit en ontwikkeling voor hele gemeenschappen. Het is een voorkoombare ziekte. Het voorkomen kost geld, het kost aanwezigheid, het kost vertrouwen. Vertrouwen dat jarenlang is opgebouwd en nu in rap tempo wordt afgebroken. Dit kan en moet anders, niet alleen incidenteel, maar ook structureel.

paragraphs.text: Fru Formand! Det er jo fuldstændig rigtigt, som kommissæren siger, at før vi er sikre alle sammen, er ingen sikre. Men jeg har samtidig lyst til også at fejre og gøre opmærksom på, at vi her i Europa faktisk har lært af det, vi har været igennem.
Vi har nu myndigheder, som holder øje; HERA, ECDC, som faktisk hver dag sørger for at sikre, at vi kan sove trygt om natten.

Mens alt det her er sket – og det har flere kommenteret på – så har USA sænket deres investeringer. USA har trukket sig fra WHO, USA har trukket sig helt ud af USAID, og i samme tidsrum har vi selvfølgelig prøvet at kompensere så godt som muligt. Vi har oprustet, og kommissæren har gjort en kæmpe indsats.

Jeg vil gerne spørge kommissæren; Kan kommissæren fortælle os, helt konkret, hvad foregår der lige nu? Hvilke aktiviteter er der sat i gang for at holde situationen under kontrol? Og frem for alt, hvad gøres der for at afhjælpe i landene netop nu?

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, dear Commissioner, one in three people does not survive Ebola. And recently the first case in France was detected. This outbreak should remind us that infectious diseases do not stop at borders. It demonstrates the need for a resilient health system worldwide.

Despite declining international help, African countries are, little by little, strengthening their own health systems through improving surveillance, regional cooperation and targeted investment. Europe should support this African‑led transition by investing in laboratories, healthcare workers and outbreak preparedness while supporting African ownership of their respective health systems.
A stronger African healthcare system is not only in Africa's interest; it's in Europe's interest. Investing in an African‑led health resilience is an investment in shared global health security.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin, verehrte Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Der Ebola-Ausbruch in Ostafrika erinnert uns daran: Gesundheit kennt keine Grenzen. Der globale Gesundheitsschutz schützt auch unsere Sicherheit.

Unsere erste Verantwortung gilt den Menschen vor Ort; sie brauchen schnelle medizinische Hilfe und starke Gesundheitssysteme. Gerade jetzt, da sich internationale Partner, insbesondere die USA, aus Teilen der Entwicklungszusammenarbeit und der globalen Gesundheitsfinanzierung zurückziehen, wächst Europas, wächst unsere Verantwortung.
Doch dieser Ausbruch ist auch eine Mahnung an Europa. Die Lehre aus Ebola lautet: Vorsorge statt Abschottung. Pandemien bekämpft man dort, wo sie entstehen, nicht erst an unseren Außengrenzen.
Aber Gesundheitspolitik ist längst auch Sicherheits‑ und Wirtschaftspolitik. Wer über resiliente Lieferketten und sichere Rohstoffpartnerschaften spricht, muss auch in globale Gesundheit investieren.

Ebola ist deshalb ein Prüfstein, ob wir globale Gesundheit als humanitäre Verantwortung und als Voraussetzung für Sicherheit und Wohlstand verstehen. Gerade jetzt, da sich andere Akteure zurückziehen, muss Europa Verantwortung übernehmen – aus Solidarität und aus kluger Vorsorge.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, l'epidemia di Ebola in Congo e in Uganda ci ricorda che le crisi sanitarie possono superare rapidamente i confini nazionali, come dimostra anche il caso confermato in Francia di un medico rientrato dal Congo, segnalato dall'Organizzazione mondiale della sanità.

La solidarietà europea non è soltanto un dovere umanitario, ma anche un investimento nella sicurezza sanitaria internazionale. Sostenendo i paesi colpiti, proteggiamo le comunità locali, riduciamo il rischio di diffusione oltre i confini e rafforziamo la capacità globale di prevenire future emergenze.

Per questo, l'Unione europea deve continuare a sostenere la sorveglianza sanitaria, la ricerca, la prevenzione e la risposta rapida alle crisi. Investire nella solidarietà, nel coordinamento e nella preparazione significa rafforzare la tutela della salute pubblica in Africa, ma anche in Europa, contribuendo al contempo a una maggiore capacità globale di prevenire future epidemie.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda is deeply worrying. While we cannot control when these outbreaks happen, we can – and must – control how we respond. Targeted emergency funding is appropriate.

At the same time, there is an endless number of crises in the world. Aid can provide temporary help, but ultimately, true safety cannot be outsourced. It starts with the institutions that are built within a country. A response to a crisis should not be to cross fingers and hope that new crises will not come. They will come, and at some point, aid money runs out. If at that point there are no institutions in the country that can step up, it is not the donor who has betrayed the people, it is their government.

interventions.speaker_label: Hadja Lahbib, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, you know, this Ebola outbreak is the 17th that occurred in the region. So it means that this epidemic outbreak didn't take us by surprise. We were prepared for that. And I have to say that when I went there in February, I saw that all the ingredients were already there to provoke this epidemic outbreak.

So it is right to say that we need structural investment, and that is exactly what we are doing. In May, we presented our humanitarian communication, which is mainly addressing the fragile context, how we can help this protracted crisis, addressing the root causes in these fragile contexts and how we can implement the famous nexus: working hand in hand with humanitarian aid, development and peace actors. And that is why we propose to strengthen our humanitarian diplomacy and to work with the long‑term vision involving our international partners, but also cooperation and development at a very early stage, because indeed, humanitarian aid cannot solve what is mainly a crisis provoked by the lack of governance and wars in this region.

And to answer your questions, dear Stine Bosse, 'What are we doing now?' As I said in my introductory remarks, we first have a very quick funding response. The eighth EU humanitarian air bridge arrived in Goma last Tuesday. Another EU air bridge is planned for South Sudan on 21 July to support the preparedness effort, and we are exploring the possibility of more EU humanitarian air bridges in the coming weeks, probably to Entebbe as it is a really strategic location.

Allow me to to end on a personal note. As a former journalist, I know the effect misinformation can have on our response to crisis. People need facts they can trust to protect themselves and their families. And that is why, when I was there in Bunia, I entered into contact. I was there to communicate for us, to European citizens, but also for local communities. And I entered into contact with traditional leaders, religious leaders to encourage them to help us to build trust with the affected communities.

And lastly, a word on the next MFF. We will have three good instruments to boost research and development and medical countermeasures: the UCPM, the European Competitiveness Fund and Horizon. I count on you for strong support for the next MFF.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Jessika Roswall, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, thank you for organising this debate on the bioeconomy and its potential to boost the EU's strategic autonomy, resilience and competitiveness. The timing could not be more relevant.

Europe is facing a changing geopolitical and economic landscape. Real wars, trade wars and climate change have turned global energy and raw material markets upside down. We often speak about our energy dependency, but we must also have a conversation about our material dependency. The bioeconomy is a part of the answer.

Every time we use bio‑based materials to produce plastic, chemicals, textiles or fertilisers, we increase our resilience and our independence. The recent crisis has highlighted just how vulnerable our economics are to external shocks. They have also reminded us that resilience is not built overnight – it requires long‑term investments, strategic partnerships and confidence in Europe's own resources.

In this context, building a competitive and sustainable bioeconomy has become an economic necessity and clear strategic opportunity for Europe. We know what the EU bioeconomy already means for citizens and businesses across Europe. I have seen it first‑hand in discussions with farmers, fishers, rural communities and innovative companies – and the numbers speak for themselves. The EU bioeconomy creates a value of around EUR 2.7 trillion. It employs 17.1 million people and corresponds to 5 % of EU GDP. And every job in the bioeconomy creates three indirect jobs in the EU.

I have no doubts that, with the right incentives, we can deliver more economic growth, environmental benefits and resilience. For the first time, we have taken steps to maximise this potential with our new EU bioeconomy strategy. We showed that the possibilities already exist in nature's design. We are not the only one who sees this. In October, the Irish Presidency will bring the world to Dublin for the Global Bioeconomy Summit, with the European Union as a committed partner. But strategies alone can only matter if they also lead to concrete actions – and this is only happening when policy, industry and finance move together. That is what I want to focus on today.

First, we aim to remove barriers that delay market entry, create uncertainty and increase administrative costs. We will look at sector‑specific regulations but also cross-cutting efforts, steered by the soon‑to‑be established Bioeconomy Regulators and Innovators' Forum. Some innovators tell me that they struggle with different national definitions of what can be considered as bio‑based. That matters a lot, of course, in terms of what legislation applies. So with the future Biotech Act II, we will streamline rules to remove bottlenecks and create a single market for these innovative products. We are also progressing work on bio‑based plastics, including the necessary preparatory studies and consultation to provide greater clarity for innovators and investors.

Second, we are taking concrete steps to bring investors to the table. The first meeting of the Bioeconomy Investment Deployment Group confirmed that the challenge is not a lack of capital, but a mismatch between available finance and the needs of bio‑based industrial projects. That is why we will work closely with the EIB, private investors and national promotional banks to better connect promising projects with the financing that they need to scale up.

During the Global Bioeconomy Summit, we will officially launch the Bio‑based Europe Alliance to mobilise private demand for bio‑based materials and products, and the alliance will gather EU companies committed to collectively purchasing bio‑based materials and products worth EUR 10 billion by 2030. We are already engaging with key industry associations and leading companies across Europe to ensure that this alliance starts delivering tangible market demands from day one. It is key to create long‑term opportunities for European bio‑based materials, products, technologies and applications, so we are also working on a buyers' club to leverage public and private investments for purchases of carbon farming credits, thus encouraging investments across value chains.

Honourable Members, building a thriving, innovative bioeconomy requires buy‑in from all Europe, from farmers to the financial sectors, from rural communities to regulators, from policymakers to researchers and innovators. So here the Parliament plays a crucial role. I really look forward to continue working with you on this strategy.

paragraphs.text: Poštovani predsjedavajući, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, farmaceutska i biotehnološka industrija strateški su sektori za Europsku uniju.

To ispravno prepoznaje Mario Draghi u svojem izvješću o konkurentnosti u kojem naglašava da će upravo inovacije u području biotehnologije i napredne proizvodnje biti ključne za budući gospodarski rast i stratešku autonomiju Europe. Europska unija danas ostvaruje trgovinski suficit od oko 220 milijardi eura u lijekovima i farmaceutskim proizvodima, što pokazuje da riječ o jednoj od naših najuspješnijih industrija. No, taj uspjeh ne smijemo uzimati zdravo za gotovo. Konkurencija je sve snažnija, Kina agresivno ulaže u proizvodnju i biotehnologiju, Indija jača svoju poziciju kao globalni proizvođač lijekova i aktivnih sastojaka, a Sjedinjene Američke Države kroz svoje industrijske politike i poticaje privlače investicije, istraživanje i razvoj iz Europe.

Ako želimo zadržati vodeću poziciju, Europa mora djelovati odlučno. Zakon o kritičnim lijekovima i predloženi Zakon o biotehnologiji važni su koraci u dobrom smjeru. Međutim, za očuvanje europske konkurentnosti potrebno je učiniti više: osigurati snažnu zaštitu intelektualnog vlasništva, ubrzati izdavanje dozvola za strateške projekte, olakšati pristup kapitalu te pomoći europskim inovativnim tvrtkama da prerastu iz uspješnih startupova u globalno konkurentne scale-up kompanije.

Upravo zato nova strategija za konkurentno i održivo gospodarstvo EU-a mora biti više od okolišne ili poljoprivredne strategije. Njezina primjena mora povezati znanost, održivu proizvodnju biomaterijala, biotehnologiju i farmaceutsku industriju. Time ćemo ojačati europsku otpornost, povećati dodatnu vrijednost naših prirodnih resursa i osigurati da inovacije nastale u Europi ostanu u Europi.
To je put prema istinski konkurentnoj, održivoj i strateški autonomnoj Europskoj uniji.

interventions.speaker_label: César Luena, en nombre del Grupo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, desde luego que la bioeconomía puede ser una gran oportunidad. Pero no podemos sustituir, comisaria, una economía basada en extraer petróleo por otra basada en extraer cada vez más recursos de la naturaleza.

Sería un error porque la biomasa no es infinita. Nuestros bosques, suelos, mares y ecosistemas tienen límites. Y respetarlos no es un freno al desarrollo, es la condición para que ese desarrollo sea duradero.

Por eso, necesitamos una bioeconomía verdaderamente circular, que aproveche mejor los residuos y los subproductos, que utilice los recursos con inteligencia y que genere más valor añadido con menos materias primas.

Tampoco podemos olvidar algo esencial: la alimentación y la biodiversidad tienen que seguir siendo prioridad. La bioeconomía nunca puede competir con la producción de alimentos ni poner más presión sobre unos ecosistemas que ya están muy tensionados.
Si queremos una Europa más fuerte y competitiva, nuestra ventaja no vendrá de producir más recursos biológicos, sino de consumir menos recursos y de crear más valor utilizando menos.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Marie-Luce Brasier-Clain, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, le Conseil a reconnu en mars dernier la bioéconomie comme un levier de souveraineté industrielle, de transition écologique et de compétitivité. Charge maintenant aux États de tirer parti de leurs abondantes ressources agricoles et forestières et des nouveaux instruments européens, notamment l’accélérateur industriel et le règlement sur les biotechnologies.

En France, la bioéconomie représente 2 millions d’emplois et 300 milliards d’euros de chiffre d’affaires par an. Mais la lecture des conclusions du Conseil interroge. On y parle de neutralité carbone et de suppression des obstacles réglementaires sans abaisser les normes, de simplification tout en installant une nouvelle bureaucratie, de protection du marché intérieur tout en prônant l’économie ouverte. Enfin, on détourne les enjeux de ce plan pour faire avancer la financiarisation de la nature et transformer l’agriculteur en simple fournisseur de services écosystémiques.
Pour faire de la bioéconomie un instrument de puissance géopolitique, l’UE doit sortir de ses dépendances stratégiques, mais aussi sortir de son inertie.

interventions.speaker_label: Elena Donazzan, a nome del gruppo ECR.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, dobbiamo riconoscere che la strategia dell'economia, della bioeconomia, è tanto.
Il termine greco "bio" riguarda il ciclo della vita.
Io mi soffermerò sul tema dei carburanti e sul loro utilizzo.

Se declinata in un'ottica di neutralità tecnologica, deve mettere anche al centro il tema dei carburanti. E parliamo di biocarburanti prodotti in Europa con materie prime europee e lavoratori europei che tengono insieme la decarbonizzazione, la sicurezza e l'occupazione.

Gli scarti animali, gli scarti dell'agricoltura, ma anche il recupero di materie prime e seconde rappresentano un buon punto di partenza per avere autonomia. Anche questo è "bio", se si considera, appunto, il ciclo della vita.

Sui carburanti, però, c'è una contraddizione. Noi oggi chiediamo – in queste ore ad Ankara, questo si dice – maggiore sforzo per la difesa, maggiore sforzo per poter essere autosufficienti, ma aerei militari che vanno a batteria non ne conosco, né carri armati, né navi, né la logistica che porta in giro i nostri mezzi e i nostri beni prodotti.
Allora dobbiamo avere un approccio della circolarità economica, garantire questo con un approccio della bioeconomia, e difendere ciò che è realmente europeo.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, for decades, Finland has championed the bioeconomy. Our economy is heavily based on that, but the bioeconomy is also so much more. Bioeconomy is an answer for several wicked problems of our time. The bioeconomy is not just wood, it is how to replace fossil-based solutions that we eventually need to get rid of with renewable local solutions based on bioeconomy and largely, yes, on wood, but also all the side streams it also generates for us.

There has been a lot of talk and goodwill with the bioeconomy, but then when it comes to the actual legislation, we constantly face contradictory goals. The Commission often presents rather restrictions on bioeconomy-driven legislation, which only supports the fossil industry and not the phasing out of it. Hopefully, we would finally find the maturity to integrate bioeconomy into the actual legislation, as this is not only a question of environment, but it is a question for the economy, security and self-sufficiency of this continent. Finally, I am very grateful for the groups that you back this discussion from the Renew initiative. It is very important theme for all of us.

interventions.speaker_label: Cristina Guarda, a nome del gruppo Verts/ALE.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, parliamo di costruire una bioeconomia europea competitiva e poi ostacoliamo una delle sue filiere più promettenti, la canapa, dove, in pochi anni, solo nell'Unione europea, la superficie coltivata è cresciuta del 60 % e la produzione di oltre l'84 %.

Non è soltanto un settore molto versatile, che fornisce materie prime per l'edilizia, il tessile, l'alimentazione, i mangimi e molti altri prodotti "bio‑based", ma anche un settore che dà agli agricoltori nuove fonti di reddito, diversificazione e quindi più resilienza, capacità di resistere alla crisi.
La nuova strategia europea per la bioeconomia deve sostenere chi lavora in questa filiera, superando gli ostacoli politici che ancora oggi ne frenano lo sviluppo.

A loro dobbiamo dare regole chiare, criteri che incentivino l'uso di materiali "bio-based" negli appalti pubblici e nelle costruzioni, investimenti – soprattutto negli impianti di prima trasformazione della fibra – e innovazione senza preconcetti.
L'Europa dispone già delle competenze, delle imprese e degli agricoltori interessati: ora serve una strategia capace di rispondere a tutto questo.

interventions.speaker_label: Anthony Smith, au nom du groupe The Left.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: au nom du groupe The Left

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, la bioéconomie est souvent présentée comme un secteur d’avenir, mais encore faut-il savoir au service de qui elle est mise en œuvre.

La nouvelle stratégie européenne de la Commission n’est, comme à son habitude, pas à la hauteur de l’enjeu. Sous couvert de compétitivité et d’innovation, elle organise la prédation généralisée du vivant. La logique est toujours la même: transformer le vivant en marchandise, exploiter davantage les forêts, les terres agricoles et la biomasse en allongeant l’exploitation des brevets. Le tout, en réduisant au maximum les normes environnementales et en remettant en cause le principe de précaution.

En réalité, cette stratégie ne répond qu’à une seule urgence: celle des intérêts des industriels et des capitalistes, en facilitant la privatisation du vivant à leur seul profit. À La France insoumise, nous refusons cette fuite en avant. Seule une stratégie fondée sur le bien commun, répondant aux besoins réels des populations, garantissant la préservation des écosystèmes, pourra faire face à la crise du climat.
Stop à l’écoblanchiment, place à la planification écologique!

paragraphs.text: Mr President, I really fully agree with Mr Sokol, that this is about growth and simplification and competitiveness for Europe. And as I see it, really, the momentum now is to make this a sustainable industry strategy. For the question on the medicine and the pharma sector, we are really pushing that we put biotech act II into place very soon.

Mr Luena, you correctly point out that the resources that we have when comes to bio are not endless, but they are renewable, they are home-grown and that is why we need to both manage them with sustainability, but also use this as the opportunity to change the decarbonisation agenda that we are into. I also want to highlight one maybe additional point on that is that another part of my portfolio is that we also need to use the circularity here.

Ms Donazzan, you mentioned defence and resilience, and this is a key point for me because as I started with my first intervention, it is about reducing our dependencies. And again, a new crisis has shown how much that costs for all of us and us as consumers.

Then on the bioeconomy, I totally agree with Ms Kulmuni from Finland, I totally agree and we know that this is not a niche. This is a big sector, I showed it a little bit with my fingers in the beginning. It is a key sector for all of Europe, a sector that we can lead if we do this right, we do this together. And I think that the time to do this is now. It's never been better or worse, but there is that we have. So absolutely, I will try to move the regulation into that security angle also.
I think that I answered Ms Guarda little bit, that for me, to harmonise and use this and link it again to circularity is exactly where I am.

Finally, to Mr Smith, as I see it, this is also an opportunity to create jobs. We already see how many jobs the bioeconomy creates in rural areas, creates for foresters, creates for farmers. So this is also again something that is beneficial for all of Europe, a win-win-win situation.

paragraphs.text: A Uachtaráin, tá áthas orm labhairt ar an ábhar tábhachtach seo.

Europe's bioeconomy represents one of our greatest untapped economic opportunities – by turning agricultural residues, forestry by-products, marine resources and organic waste into high-value products, we can reduce our dependence on fossil-based materials while creating new jobs, new industries, and new income streams for rural communities. We need to frame the bioeconomy as a critical element of Europe's industrial policy, innovation policy and competitiveness policy. It strengthens European strategic autonomy by producing more of the materials, chemicals, fuels and ingredients we need here in Europe from resources we already have.

I therefore welcome investments such as Ireland's new National Biorefinery Pilot Plant in County Monaghan, which helps researchers, SMEs and industry from across the country to transform promising ideas into commercially viable products, bridging the gap between laboratory research and market deployment. If Europe is serious about competitiveness, circularity and supporting our rural economy, then we must put the bioeconomy at the heart of our industrial strategy, invest in innovation and give Europe's entrepreneurs the tools they need to scale-up and succeed.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Die Bioökonomie kann oder wird ein wichtiger Baustein für eine wettbewerbsfähige und unabhängigere Europäische Union sein, aber mehr Unabhängigkeit bedeutet nicht, dass wir einfach Biomaterialien produzieren und fossile durch biobasierte Materialien ersetzen. Schon heute stehen unsere Ökosysteme unter enormem Druck; die Bioökonomie darf deshalb nicht einfach das alte lineare Wirtschaftsmodell mit einem grünen Etikett fortsetzen.

Unsere Antwort muss – die Kommissarin hat es auch schon gesagt – eine Kreislauf-Bioökonomie sein, weniger Ressourcenverbrauch und eine klare Orientierung an der Abfallhierarchie. Unsere Chance liegt nämlich darin, mit weniger Ressourcen mehr Wert zu schaffen. Das Kreislaufwirtschaftsgesetz, das zweite Biotech-Gesetz bieten dafür wichtige Möglichkeiten – durch eine stärkere Kaskadennutzung von Biomasse, durch klare Kriterien, wann biobasierte Materialien über ihren gesamten Lebenszyklus tatsächlich einen Vorteil bringen, durch Quoten für den Einsatz dieser Materialien aus europäischer Produktion und durch die Staffelung von Abfallgebühren entsprechend der tatsächlichen Umweltfreundlichkeit der eingesetzten Materialien.

Ich bin überzeugt, so schaffen wir eine Bioökonomie, die nachhaltiger ist, die Europas Wettbewerbsfähigkeit stärkt durch Innovation, durch Ressourceneffizienz und durch weniger Abhängigkeit von globalen Rohstoffmärkten.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Mr President, members, a competitive and sustainable bioeconomy is a strategic necessity. Our recent experience of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz makes that all the more clear. The EU's vision for the bioeconomy is that, by 2040, bio-based construction products like biochemicals, textiles, fertilisers, plastics and so forth will all be widely deployed across our Union. These are to be fossil-free alternatives that create stable new income streams for citizens.

Looking specifically at the potential of fertilisers, we see that the bio-based fertilisers can cut our dependence on imports, lower our carbon footprint and turn agricultural residues and organic waste into real economic value. That is why, when the Commission evaluates the fertilising products regulation, it must ask whether it is delivering market access for bio-based fertilisers appropriately. If not, we need to see action now. We need to see these products fast-tracked to the market. It's a rare case where everyone can win and we can – and have to at this stage because of what I mentioned earlier – grab that opportunity with both hands.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, ogni giorno nelle nostre case, nelle mense, nei supermercati e nelle aziende agricole milioni di tonnellate di cibo finiscono nella spazzatura.

In quei materiali c'è già una parte del futuro dell'Europa: quello che oggi scartiamo può diventare energia pulita, fertilizzanti naturali, nuovi materiali compostabili, nuove imprese, nuovi posti di lavoro.
La bioeconomia è una grande politica industriale, non solo ambientale. È una scelta di libertà, perché significa dipendere meno dalle materie prime importate e valorizzare ciò che già produciamo.
L'Europa possiede competenze, ricerca e imprese capaci di guidare questa trasformazione, ma siamo lenti.

Gli scarti organici non sono un problema da eliminare, ma una risorsa da valorizzare. Dobbiamo rendere più efficienti i nostri sistemi di raccolta e di riciclo in tutta Europa e promuovere i materiali compostabili, che rappresentano davvero la soluzione migliore. Oggi troppe filiere "bio‑based" restano bloccate da ostacoli burocratici che frenano l'innovazione.
In un mondo in cui le materie prime sono sempre più rare e più contese, continuare a sprecare risorse è un lusso che l'Europa non si può più permettere.
La bioeconomia non è un sogno per il futuro, è un'opportunità concreta per costruire un'Europa più forte, più competitiva e più autonoma.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, η ευρωπαϊκή βιοοικονομία μπορεί να αποτελέσει φυσικά σημαντικό εργαλείο για την πράσινη μετάβαση, την καινοτομία, τη βιομηχανική ανταγωνιστικότητα και τη στρατηγική αυτονομία της Ευρώπης. Όμως πρέπει να είμαστε σε κάτι πολύ ξεκάθαροι: Η βιοοικονομία δεν μπορεί να γίνει μια νέα μορφή πίεσης πάνω στη γη, στα δάση, στο νερό και στη βιοποικιλότητα γενικότερα. Δεν αρκεί να αντικαταστήσουμε τα ορυκτά υλικά δηλαδή με βιολογικούς πόρους, αν αυτό οδηγεί σε υπερεκμετάλλευση οικοσυστημάτων ή σε ανταγωνισμό με την παραγωγή τροφίμων.

Χρειαζόμαστε μια βιοοικονομία κυκλική, προπαντός δίκαιη και πραγματικά βιώσιμη, με προτεραιότητα στην υψηλή προστιθέμενη αξία και στις τοπικές αλυσίδες παραγωγής. Οι αγρότες, οι δασοκόμοι, οι αλιείς και οι παράκτιες κοινότητες δεν πρέπει να είναι απλώς προμηθευτές πρώτων υλών, πρέπει να είναι συμμέτοχοι στην αξία που δημιουργείται —και ιδιαίτερα στη Μεσόγειο, όπου η ξηρασία, η λειψυδρία και η απώλεια εδαφών επιδεινώνονται. Η βιοοικονομία πρέπει να συνδεθεί με την ανθεκτικότητα, την προστασία των φυσικών πόρων και την κοινωνική δικαιοσύνη.
Στρατηγική αυτονομία λοιπόν; Ναι, αλλά μέσα στα όρια της φύσης.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, Europe has a hidden strength: our bioeconomy, our bio-based solutions. What is this? Well, it is the power of the new and the very old. The power of the gigantic and the very, very small. The largest trees in our forests and the smallest, smallest microorganisms. They feed, they heal, they ferment and they build.

The bioeconomy contributes almost EUR 1 trillion annually to our Union, more than 8 % of GDP, and supports 17 % of our jobs. We must use this strategic asset to build for our future food security and to deliver our clean transition.
Europe's position is under pressure. The US and China move very fast. Now our Europe needs a strong Biotech Act II to create lead markets, to buy greener, to simplify how we regulate.
